final answer
I now have the complete picture. Here's the full trace. # Stock item lifecycle: Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice ## Stage 1 — Sales Order (commitment only; no stock, no ledger impact) **File:** `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` — `class SalesOrder(SellingController)` The Sales Order is purely commercial. `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (line 450) does **not** call `update_stock_ledger()` or `make_gl_entries()` — no Stock Ledger Entry (SLE) and no GL Entry is ever produced. It only: - `update_prevdoc_status()` / `update_reserved_qty()` (→ `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty`, `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py`), and optionally `create_stock_reservation_entries()` when `reserve_stock` is set. - Registers a `status_updater` chain (inherited via `StatusUpdater`, `erpnext/controllers/status_updater.py`) so that later Delivery Notes and stock-updating Sales Invoices will fill `Sales Order Item.delivered_qty` / `per_delivered`, and invoices will fill `billed_amt` / `per_billed`. ## Stage 2 — Delivery Note (stock moves; expense is booked — possibly into a holding account) **Files:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py` (`class DeliveryNote(SellingController)`), `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`, `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py`, `erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/billing_status.py` `DeliveryNote.on_submit()` (line 481) runs, in order: 1. **`update_prevdoc_status()`** — the first `status_updater` entry in `DeliveryNote.__init__` updates `Sales Order Item.delivered_qty`/`per_delivered`/`delivery_status`. Note its `second_source_dt = "Sales Invoice Item"` with `second_source_extra_cond: ... and update_stock = 1` — the SO counts delivery from *either* a DN *or* an invoice with "Update Stock". 2. **`update_billing_status()`** → `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status` → `update_billed_amount_based_on_so()` and `StockController.update_billing_percentage()`, which set `Delivery Note Item.billed_amt` and DN `per_billed` (status "To Bill" → "Partially Billed" → "Completed"). 3. **`update_stock_ledger()`** (`SellingController.update_stock_ledger`, selling_controller.py line 676) — builds outgoing SLEs via `get_item_list()` → `get_sle_for_source_warehouse()` → `make_sl_entries()` → `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries` → `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.make_sl_entries`. When enabled: - `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account()` (l.438–479) forces stock items *not yet* linked to an invoice to use the **SDBNB balance-sheet account** as `expense_account`, so the DN posts Dr **SDBNB** / Cr Stock — no P&L impact before billing. - `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries()` (l.164–253) then, for DN-linked items where `_is_sdbnb_reversal()` confirms the DN used the SDBNB account, posts **Dr COGS (`item.expense_account`) / Cr SDBNB**, valued from the DN's SLE (`stock_value_difference / actual_qty × item.stock_qty`). The expense still lands **once** — at billing, funded from the DN's valuation. **Layer 4 — no duplicate delivery/billing quantity.** `StatusUpdater.validate_qty()`/`update_qty()` (status_updater.py l.266/533) with `overflow_type: "delivery"` and the `second_source_extra_cond: "… and update_stock = 1"` clauses in `DeliveryNote.__init__` (l.170–175) ensure an SI counts toward SO `delivered_qty` *only if it moved stock itself* — exactly the anti-double-count rule. Over-billing is blocked by `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` (sales_invoice.py l.351–353; `erpnext/accounts/services/billing_validation.py`). **Net effect:** SO (nothing) → DN (Dr COGS-or-SDBNB / Cr Stock, from its SLEs) → SI (Dr Debtors / Cr Income; plus Dr COGS / Cr SDBNB if SDBNB is on). The COGS pair is emitted by exactly one voucher — the DN — with the SI's `update_stock` checkbox disabled for DN-linked rows; reversals on cancel are symmetric via `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` / `make_reverse_gl_entries()`.

Here's the full trace. # Stock lifecycle: Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice ## Stage 1 — Sales Order: commitment only, zero accounting `SalesOrder` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py`, extends `SellingController`) posts **no GL entries and no stock ledger entries**. `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (L450) does only operational bookkeeping: - `update_prevdoc_status()` — maintains `delivered_qty` / `billed_qty` counters on `Sales Order Item` via `AccountsController.status_updater` - `update_reserved_qty()` → `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py`) — recalculates `reserved_qty` on **Bin** - `create_stock_reservation_entries()` — only when `reserve_stock` is checked; creates `Stock Reservation Entry` records that *earmark* stock without moving it (consumed later by `DeliveryNote.validate_against_stock_reservation_entries()`, L544) - `check_credit_limit()` ## Stage 2 — Delivery Note: stock moves, COGS is booked here `DeliveryNote` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py`, L17): - **validate** (L276): `validate_with_previous_doc()` enforces consistency with the SO/SI rows (`against_sales_order`/`so_detail`/`si_detail`); `validate_expense_account()` (L438) resolves the COGS account — and, if Company "Stock Delivered But Not Billed" accounting is enabled, parks it in the SDBNB account until invoicing. - **on_submit** (L481): `update_prevdoc_status()` → updates SO `delivered_qty`/status; `update_billing_status()` → `BillingStatusService` + `StockController.update_billing_percentage()` (`per_billed`); then, in strict order: `update_stock_ledger()` → `SellingController.update_stock_ledger()` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`, L676) → `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries()` — writes outgoing SLEs (negative `actual_qty` with computed `stock_value_difference`); then `make_gl_entries()`; then `repost_future_sle_and_gle()`. - **COGS entry**: `StockController.make_gl_entries()` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, L178) → `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries()` (L433) → **`DeliveryNoteGLComposer`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py`) → `BaseStockGLComposer.compose()` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`). The composer fetches the voucher's own SLEs via `StockLedgerService.get_stock_ledger_details()` (keyed by `voucher_detail_no` = child row name) and, per item row, posts the pair: - **Dr Inventory (warehouse asset account)** = `sle.stock_value_difference` - **Cr item.expense_account (COGS)** = `-sle.stock_value_difference` For an outgoing delivery this nets to the classic **Dr COGS / Cr Stock**. `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` itself adds nothing extra — it only relaxes `enforce_pl_expense_account = False` (delivery differences may hit a balance-sheet account on internal transfers). ## Stage 3 — Sales Invoice: revenue booked, COGS *not* re-booked The invoice is built by `make_sales_invoice()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py`, L62): it maps `Delivery Note Item.name → dn_detail` and `parent → delivery_note`, pulls only pending qty (`qty − invoiced − returned`, FIFO-aware), and crucially **never sets `update_stock`** — it stays 0. `SalesInvoice.on_submit()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py`, L421): `check_prev_docstatus()` (L1025 — throws if the linked DN isn't submitted), `update_prevdoc_status()`, `update_billing_status_in_dn()` (L1084 — writes `billed_amt` back to `Delivery Note Item` and calls `dn.update_billing_percentage()`, flipping the DN to "Completed"), then `make_gl_entries()` (L1030) → `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`). ## The "exactly once" mechanism The whole guarantee lives in **`SalesInvoiceGLComposer.make_item_gl_entries()`** (L346–375): ```python # expense account gl entries if cint(doc.update_stock) and erpnext.is_perpetual_inventory_enabled(doc.company): gl_entries += super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries() ``` 1. **DN-billed invoice (`update_stock=0`)**: the stock/expense block is skipped entirely. The composer books only Cr `income_account` per item, Dr `debit_to` (AR), taxes, discounts, POS/write-off entries. No COGS — it was already booked by the DN's SLE-driven pair at delivery time. 2. **Standalone invoice (`update_stock=1`, no DN)**: `on_submit` runs `update_stock_ledger()` (SLEs created by the SI itself), and the unbound `super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()` call routes into `StockController.get_gl_entries()` → `BaseStockGLComposer.compose()` against the *SI's own* SLEs → Dr COGS / Cr Stock, exactly once. 3. **Mixing is impossible**: `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note()` (L904) hard-throws — *"Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes"* — if `update_stock` is checked while any item carries a `delivery_note` link. (`is_subcontracted()` L1191 additionally forces `update_stock = 0`.) `BillingValidationService.validate_multiple_billing("Delivery Note", "dn_detail", "amount")` separately prevents over-billing the same DN row. 4. **The SDBNB refinement** — for the timing gap you asked about: with `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` on, `DeliveryNote.validate_expense_account()` sets the DN's expense account to the **SDBNB holding account** (balance sheet, not P&L) at delivery. Then `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries()` (L164) with helpers `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item()`, `_is_sdbnb_reversal()` and `_append_sdbnb_gl_entries()` reclassifies at invoice time: **Cr SDBNB / Dr item.expense_account** for `valuation_rate × stock_qty` (valuation taken from the DN's SLE). P&L COGS is still recognized exactly once — just on the invoice date — and the `dn_expense_account != item.expense_account` check plus the "SDBNB account cannot be used for items linked to a Sales Invoice" throw in `validate_expense_account` prevent it from ever leaking into a second expense hit. **Summary of files/classes:** `SalesOrder`/`SalesOrderStockReservation` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/…`), `DeliveryNote` + `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` + `BillingStatusService` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/…`), `SalesInvoice` + `SalesInvoiceGLComposer` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/…`), shared plumbing in `SellingController` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py`), `StockController` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`), `BaseStockGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`), and `StockLedgerService` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py`), all posted through `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py: make_gl_entries`.

I now have the complete picture across all three doctypes. Here is the full trace. # The lifecycle: SO → DN → SI ## Class hierarchy (the key to the whole design) All three doctypes share one chain, which is what lets the same stock/GL machinery be reused — or *skipped* — per document: ``` Sales Order ─┐ Delivery Note ─┤→ SellingController → StockController → AccountsController → StatusUpdater Sales Invoice ─┘ ``` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:19`, `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py`) ## 1. Sales Order — a commitment, no ledger impact `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450`) only calls `update_prevdoc_status()`, `check_credit_limit()` and `update_reserved_qty()` → `SalesOrderStockReservation.update_reserved_qty()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/services/reservation.py:35`). **No Stock Ledger Entries, no GL entries** — the SO only: - reserves stock via *Stock Reservation Entries* (voucher_type "Sales Order"), earmarked in the Bin; - carries the link keys the downstream docs use: `Sales Order Item.name` (= `so_detail`) and the SO name (= `against_sales_order` on DN Item / `sales_order` on SI Item). ## 2. Delivery Note — the stock event AND the cost event `DeliveryNote(SellingController)` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17`): - **`validate()`** (:276): `so_required()` (if Selling Settings demand it), `validate_with_previous_doc()` (:299 — rows must match the referenced SO/SI), `validate_warehouse()`, and **`validate_expense_account()`** (:438) — for every stock item not linked to an invoice, sets `item.expense_account` to the company's **"Stock Delivered But Not Billed" (SDBNB)** account when `enable_stock_delivered_but_not_billed` is on (and throws if SDBNB is used on rows *already* linked to an SI). - **`on_submit()`** (:481), in order: 1. `update_prevdoc_status()` + `update_billing_status()` → `BillingStatusService` — driven by the `status_updater` built in `__init__` (:157-233): DN Item → SO Item `delivered_qty`/`per_delivered`, with `second_source_extra_cond: "... update_stock = 1"` so SI rows only count as delivery when that invoice itself posted stock; DN Item → SI Item `delivered_qty` (with `no_allowance: 1`). 2. `update_stock_reservation_entries()` (SellingController:930) — marks reserved qty as delivered. 3. **`update_stock_ledger()`** (SellingController:676) → `get_item_list()` (includes Product-Bundle `packed_items`) → `get_sle_for_source_warehouse()` (:708) → `StockLedgerService.make_sl_entries` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py`) — negative `actual_qty` SLEs, with `incoming_rate`/`stock_value_difference` from `get_incoming_rate`/`get_valuation_rate` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py`). 4. **`make_gl_entries()`** (inherited `StockController.make_gl_entries`, stock_controller.py:178) → `DeliveryNote.get_gl_entries()` (:433) → `DeliveryNoteGLComposer` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/services/gl_composer.py:7`, which only relaxes the P&L check) → **`BaseStockGLComposer.compose()`** (`erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py:27`). For each item row's SLEs this posts the canonical pair: - **Credit** the warehouse's inventory account, amount = `sle.stock_value_difference` (negative on outward); - **Debit** `item.expense_account` (COGS — or the SDBNB provisional account, see §3) with `-1 × stock_value_difference`. 5. `repost_future_sle_and_gle()` (StockController:360) — if valuation changed retroactively, downstream SLEs/GLEs are reposted so COGS stays accurate. Result: at DN submission, inventory is relieved and the cost of goods is already on the P&L. The DN sits at status "To Bill" with no receivable/income. ## 3. Sales Invoice — billing only (normally), stock+COGS only when it *is* the delivery `SalesInvoice(SellingController)` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62`): - **Creation from the DN**: `make_sales_invoice()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py:62`) maps `dn_detail`/`delivery_note`/`so_detail`/`sales_order`, computes pending qty from `get_invoiced_qty_map`/`get_returned_qty_map`, and **never sets `update_stock`** — the invoice arrives with `update_stock = 0`. - **`validate()`** (:289): `so_dn_required()` (:854 — DN reference can satisfy the requirement only when `update_stock` is *off*); `validate_with_previous_doc()` (:784 — rows must match `delivery_note`/`dn_detail` and `so_detail`); if `update_stock` → `validate_warehouse()` (:331); then **`validate_delivery_note()` (:904)** — the hard guard: *"Stock cannot be updated against the following Delivery Notes"*. An invoice referencing a DN is simply not allowed to also check `update_stock`. (`check_prev_docstatus()` :1016 additionally requires the referenced SO/DN to be submitted at submit time.) - **`on_submit()`** (:421): - `update_status_updater_args()` (:594): SI Item → SO Item `billed_amt`/`per_billed` always; SO Item `delivered_qty` **only under the `extra_cond` `update_stock = 1`**; Pick List Item delivered qty likewise. - `update_prevdoc_status()` + `update_billing_status_in_dn()` (:1084) — flips the DN's `per_billed`/status (To Bill → Completed) via `StatusUpdater`. - `if self.update_stock == 1:` → **`update_stock_ledger()`** (SellingController:676) — SLEs only here; then after GL, `repost_future_sle_and_gle()`. - **`make_gl_entries()`** (:1030) → `SalesInvoice.get_gl_entries()` (:1070) → `SalesInvoiceGLComposer.compose()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/services/gl_composer.py:22`): - `make_customer_gl_entry` (:255) — Debit Debtors; - `make_item_gl_entries` (:346) — **Credit income account per item; and the expense block is gated at :374**: `if cint(doc.update_stock) and perpetual inventory enabled: gl_entries += super(SalesInvoice, doc).get_gl_entries()` — i.e. it re-enters the *same* `StockController.get_gl_entries` → `BaseStockGLComposer` the DN used, producing the inventory-credit/COGS-debit pair **only when the invoice itself is the delivery**. With `update_stock = 0`, zero stock/expense entries are produced. - `stock_delivered_but_not_billed_gl_entries()` (:164, `_get_sdbnb_booking_for_item` :174, `_is_sdbnb_reversal` :212): when SDBNB accounting is enabled and the invoice bills a DN whose rows were expensed to the SDBNB account, it posts **Credit SDBNB / Debit the item's real COGS account**, valued at the DN's `stock_value_difference` per unit — a *reclassification* of the cost already booked by the DN, not a second expense. # How COGS is booked exactly once (not twice) The invariant is: **exactly one document per item-qty may post the stock movement, and COGS is a mechanical byproduct of that movement's SLE.** It is enforced in layers: 1. **Ownership by `update_stock`** — `update_stock_ledger()` runs on DN submit unconditionally (delivery_note.py:511), but on SI submit only inside `if self.update_stock == 1` (sales_invoice.py:443-453). The COGS GL pair (BaseStockGLComposer) is generated from those SLEs on both paths, so whichever doc moves stock books the cost. 2. **Mapper default** — `make_sales_invoice` (delivery_note/mapper.py:62) never sets `update_stock`, so the standard DN→SI invoice is billing-only: Debtors + Income; the cost already sits in COGS from the DN. 3. **Hard validation** — `SalesInvoice.validate_delivery_note()` (sales_invoice.py:904, called at :335) throws if `update_stock = 1` on any invoice whose items reference Delivery Notes — making the double-posting combination structurally impossible, not merely discouraged. 4. **SDBNB two-step (no duplication, only relocation)** — with Company → *Enable Stock Delivered But Not Billed*: DN debits the provisional SDBNB account (delivery_note.py:474-475); the SI reclassifies it to true COGS (credit SDBNB / debit expense account, gl_composer.py:164-253). Net P&L expense still occurs exactly once; `validate_expense_account` (:457) even forbids SDBNB surviving on invoice-linked DN rows. 5. **Quantity-level idempotence in the SO** — both `status_updater` maps count delivery toward the SO only via DN rows or SI rows whose parent has `update_stock = 1` (`second_source_extra_cond`/`extra_cond` in delivery_note.py:174-175 and sales_invoice.py:616-617), and `SellingController.get_already_delivered_qty()` (selling_controller.py:442) sums DN qty plus **only** SI qty where `si.update_stock == 1` when checking over-delivery — the two sources can never both apply to the same `so_detail`. 6. **Re-billing prevention** — `get_invoiced_qty_map` (mapper.py:21) filters out fully-invoiced DN rows, and DN Item → SI Item `delivered_qty` with `no_allowance: 1` blocks over-billing; on cancel, `on_cancel` reverses SLEs and GL (`make_reverse_gl_entries`, sales_invoice.py:1053-1068, delivery_note.py:528-533) symmetrically. **Net result:** the stock-out SLE exists once (on the DN, or on an `update_stock` SI that never references a DN), and therefore the COGS debit exists once. A normal DN-then-SI sequence books *Debit COGS / Credit Stock* at delivery and *Debit Debtors / Credit Income* at billing; the invoice's only stock-related GL job is, optionally, moving that cost from the provisional SDBNB account into real COGS.

I now have the complete picture. Here is the full trace of the subcontracting flow: # Subcontracting flow: raw material → supplier → Subcontracting Order → Subcontracting Receipt (cost roll-up) ## 0. Origin — Subcontracted Purchase Order - `PurchaseOrder` (`is_subcontracted` flag) — `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py` - `SubcontractingService` (`validate_fg_item_for_subcontracting`, `set_service_items_for_finished_goods`, `auto_create_subcontracting_order`, `update_subcontracting_order_status`) — `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/services/subcontracting.py` - On PO submit, `auto_create_subcontracting_order()` calls the whitelisted mapper **`make_subcontracting_order()` → `get_mapped_subcontracting_order()`** (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/mapper.py`), which maps PO items into `Subcontracting Order Service Item` rows and, in `post_process`, calls **`SubcontractingOrder.populate_items_table()`** — this expands each service item into a finished-good item row using the **`Subcontracting BOM`** (`finished_good_bom`, or the item's `default_bom`) and computes the `subcontracting_conversion_factor`. ## 1. Subcontracting Order — defining what raw material the company owes the supplier `class SubcontractingOrder(SubcontractingController)` — `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py` - **validate**: `validate_purchase_order_for_subcontracting` (PO must be submitted & subcontracted), `validate_items` (inherited: requires `is_stock_item` + `is_sub_contracted_item` + active BOM, and caps qty via **`get_pending_subcontracted_quantity()`** in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`), `validate_service_items`, `validate_supplied_items`. - **Raw-material expansion**: inherited `SubcontractingController.validate()` → **`create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received(raw_material_table="supplied_items")` → `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()` → `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items()`** → **`_get_materials_from_bom()`** explodes the item's BOM (handling phantom items and exploded items) into `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` rows with `reserve_warehouse` (set by `__update_reserve_warehouse` from `set_reserve_warehouse`). - **Cost roll-up on the order**: `calculate_service_costs` (→ `service_cost_per_qty`), `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount` (→ `rm_cost_per_qty` = BOM RM cost ÷ BOM qty), `calculate_additional_costs` (→ `additional_cost_per_qty`), `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` (`rate = rm + service + additional`). - **on_submit**: `update_status()` (status → Open), `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po()` (writes `Purchase Order Item.subcontracted_qty`), **`reserve_raw_materials()`** (creates `StockReservation` entries in `erpnext.stock.doctype.stock_reservation_entry`); bin state updated by `update_ordered_qty_for_subcontracting` / `update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` → `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py`). ## 2. Movement of raw material to the supplier — Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor" - Mapper: **`make_rm_stock_entry()`** (`@frappe.whitelist`, in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`; UI wrapper `get_items_from_subcontract_order` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`). Its `post_process` builds `Stock Entry` rows with **`s_warehouse` = item `warehouse`/`reserve_warehouse` (company's own warehouse)** and **`t_warehouse` = `Subcontracting Order.supplier_warehouse`** (a company-owned "supplier" WIP warehouse), sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"`, links each row back to the order via **`sco_rm_detail`** and tags `subcontracted_item`/`main_item_code`; over-transfer is bounded by `over_transfer_allowance` and `required_qty − total_supplied_qty`. - Behavior class: **`SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`), selected by `StockEntry._configure_purpose_class()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py`). - `validate_subcontract_order` enforces qty limits in both backflush modes: `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` / `_get_required_qty_for_bom` / `_validate_transfer_qty` (BOM mode), `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer` (transferred-qty mode). - `on_submit`/`on_cancel` → **`update_subcontract_order_supplied_items()`** → `get_supplied_items()` aggregates `transfer_qty` per `sco_rm_detail` and writes `supplied_qty / returned_qty / total_supplied_qty` back to `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`, plus `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting()` on the Bin. - `StockEntry.on_submit` also runs `reserve_stock_for_subcontracting()` (moves Stock Reservation Entries from the SCO to the transfer) and **`update_subcontracting_order_status()`** → `set_subcontracting_order_status` → `SubcontractingOrder.update_status()`, which flips the SCO to *Material Transferred / Partial Material Transferred* based on `supplied_items.supplied_qty`. - Unused material comes back via **`get_materials_from_supplier()` → `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract()` + `add_items_in_ste()`** (subcontracting_controller.py) — a `Material Transfer` `is_return` Stock Entry built from `get_available_materials()`. ## 3. Receipt of finished goods — Subcontracting Receipt - Mapper: **`make_subcontracting_receipt()` → `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt()`** (subcontracting_order.py) maps SCO → SCR, carrying `subcontracting_order_item`, `bom`, `supplier_warehouse`, and applying the BOM's `process_loss_percentage`. (UI buttons wired in `subcontracting_order.js`.) - `class SubcontractingReceipt(SubcontractingController)` — `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py`. - **Tracking against the Subcontracting Order**: each `Subcontracting Receipt Item` carries `subcontracting_order` + `subcontracting_order_item`; on submit, `status_updater` (set in `__init__`) pushes `received_qty` into `Subcontracting Order Item.received_qty` and recomputes `Subcontracting Order.per_received` (`overflow_type: "receipt"`); `set_subcontracting_order_status()` then re-evaluates the SCO status (*Partially Received / Completed*), and `update_ordered_and_reserved_qty()` refreshes the SCO's bins (throwing `InvalidStatusError` if the SCO is Closed/Cancelled). ## 4. Reconciliation of transferred raw material against the SCO (backflush) All in `SubcontractingController` (`erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py`), driven by `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items()`: - **`get_available_materials()`** — builds `available_materials` keyed `(rm_item_code, main_item_code, subcontracting_order)`: - `__get_transferred_items()` queries submitted **Stock Entries with `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"` (or return `Material Transfer`)** where `Stock Entry.subcontracting_order` is in the receipt's orders — this is the actual link between the material transfer and the SCO; - serial/batch availability via `get_voucher_wise_serial_batch_from_bundle()`; - `__update_consumed_materials()` subtracts quantities already consumed by prior Subcontracting Receipts (reads `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item` via `__get_received_items`/`__get_consumed_items`). - **`__set_supplied_or_received_items()`** allocates `consumed_qty` per FG row — from BOM (`_get_materials_from_bom`) when `backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on = "BOM"`, else proportionally from transferred stock (`__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer` / `qty_to_be_received`) — creating `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item` rows, with serial/batch bundles via `__set_serial_and_batch_bundle()` → `SerialBatchCreation`. - Validation that consumption matches what was actually supplied: `__validate_supplied_or_received_items()` → `__validate_batch_no()` / `__validate_serial_no()` (throws *"Batch/Serial Nos not supplied against the Subcontracting Order"*), and on submit **`validate_bom_required_qty()` + `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty()`** (`BOMQuantityError`) enforces BOM-required quantities. - **Consumed qty written back to the order**: `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()` → `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()` sets `consumed_qty` on `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` (called from both `on_submit` and `on_cancel`). ## 5. Cost roll-up & ledger reconciliation on the Subcontracting Receipt - **RM valuation**: `set_valuation_rate_for_rm()` re-prices each consumed RM at `supplier_warehouse` with **`get_incoming_rate()`** (`erpnext/stock/utils.py`) — i.e., consumption is valued at what the stock cost when it sits at the supplier; also `set_rate_for_supplied_items()`, `__set_rate_for_serial_and_batch_bundle()` (bundle `avg_rate`), `update_rate_for_supplied_items()`/`set_batch_for_supplied_items()` for `use_serial_batch_fields`. - **FG cost roll-up**: `set_missing_values()` → `calculate_additional_costs()` + **`calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`**: `rm_supp_cost` = Σ consumed RM amounts; `rm_cost_per_qty = rm_supp_cost / received_qty`; adds `service_cost_per_qty`, `additional_cost_per_qty`, `secondary_items_cost_per_qty` (from **`get_secondary_items()`**, with scrap valued via `get_valuation_rate` in `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`) and `landed_cost_voucher_amount` (LCV via `StockController.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`); `item.rate` = sum of all components; amount applies the BOM `cost_allocation_per`. - **Stock ledger** (`update_stock_ledger()`, overridden in the controller): FG enters `item.warehouse` with `incoming_rate = item.rate` and **`recalculate_rate = 1`**; **`make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse()`** posts the consumed RM out of `supplier_warehouse` (`actual_qty = -consumed_qty`). - **Ledger⇄document cost reconciliation**: `StockLedger.get_dynamic_incoming_outgoing_rate()` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`) re-reads the rate from the voucher for `recalculate_rate` entries (`rate_field = "rate"` on `Subcontracting Receipt Item`); for the negative RM entry, `update_outgoing_rate_on_transaction()` → **`update_rate_on_subcontracting_receipt()`** writes the realized `outgoing_rate` back into `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item.rate/amount` and re-runs `calculate_items_qty_and_amount()` — closing the loop between actual ledger valuation and the document's cost roll-up. - **GL entries**: `get_gl_entries()` → **`SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer`** (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`, on `BaseStockGLComposer`): debits the FG inventory account with the SLE `stock_value_diff`, credits `expense_account` with `stock_value_diff − service_cost`, credits `service_expense_account` with service cost; **`rm_supp_cost` entries** move the consumed RM cost out of the supplier-warehouse inventory account into expense; additional-cost and divisional-loss (`item.amount − stock_value_diff` → `stock_adjustment_account`) entries; LCV entries via `_make_item_gl_entries_for_lcv()`. - Final hooks in `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit`: `update_stock_reservation_entries`, `repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `update_status` (Completed), **`auto_create_purchase_receipt()` → `make_purchase_receipt()`** (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py`) which creates the billing Purchase Receipt against the original PO (`is_subcontracted=1`), and `update_job_card()`. **Key files**: `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` (the spine), `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`, `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/subcontracting_receipt.py` (+ `mapper.py`, `services/gl_composer.py`), `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`, `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py`, `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`, plus the PO mappers in `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/`.

Below is the complete end‑to‑end trace of the subcontracting flow in ERPNext, with the concrete classes/functions and files at every hop. ## Core artifacts | Artifact | File | |---|---| | `SubcontractingController` (shared base) | `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` | | `SubcontractingOrder` (+ Item / Service Item / Supplied Item) | `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/` | | `SubcontractingReceipt` (+ Item / Supplied Item) | `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/` | | `Subcontracting BOM` (FG ↔ service item mapping) | `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_bom/subcontracting_bom.py` | | Stock Entry service classes for subcontracting | `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py` | | Receipt GL composer | `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` | Key traceability fields: `Subcontracting Order Item → Subcontracting Receipt Item.subcontracting_order_item`, and `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item.name → Stock Entry Detail.sco_rm_detail → Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item`. ## 1. Purchase Order (service item) → Subcontracting Order - `SubcontractingService` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/services/subcontracting.py`): `validate_fg_item_for_subcontracting`, `set_service_items_for_finished_goods` (resolves the service item for each FG via `get_subcontracting_boms_for_finished_goods` in `subcontracting_bom.py`), `auto_create_subcontracting_order`, `update_subcontracting_order_status`. Wired from `PurchaseOrder.validate` / `on_submit` in `erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py` (`set_service_items_for_finished_goods`, line 490). - `make_subcontracting_order` → `get_mapped_subcontracting_order` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/mapper.py`, lines 221–330) maps PO → `Subcontracting Order`; its `post_process` calls **`SubcontractingOrder.populate_items_table()`** (`subcontracting_order.py`, 238–298), which creates FG item rows, picks the BOM (`Subcontracting BOM.finished_good_bom` or `Item.default_bom`) and defaults `supplier_warehouse` from the Job Card's WIP warehouse. - Raw-materials table: `SubcontractingController.validate` → **`create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")`** → `set_materials_for_subcontracted_items` → `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` → `__set_supplied_or_received_items` → **`_get_materials_from_bom`** (lines 560–609; reads `BOM Item`, excludes `sourced_by_supplier`, expands phantom items) → `__add_supplied_or_received_item` (695–734) appends `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` rows with `required_qty` + `reserve_warehouse`. - Costing on the order: `SubcontractingOrder.set_missing_values` (183–187) → `calculate_service_costs` (`service_cost_per_qty` from the service item), `calculate_supplied_items_qty_and_amount` (`rm_cost_per_qty` from BOM), `calculate_items_qty_and_amount` (`rate = rm + service + additional`). - On submit (`SubcontractingOrder.on_submit`): `update_status` ("Open" → later "Partial/Material Transferred" from `supplied_qty`), `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po`, `reserve_raw_materials` (Stock Reservation Entries). Bin reservation is recomputed by `Bin.update_reserved_qty_for_sub_contracting` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/bin/bin.py`, 142–215). ## 2. Raw materials → supplier: Stock Entry "Send to Subcontractor" - The SCO form button (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.js`, line 698) calls **`make_rm_stock_entry(subcontract_order, rm_items, order_doctype, target_doc)`** in `erpnext/controllers/subcontracting_controller.py` (1343–1466). Its `post_process`: - sets `purpose = "Send to Subcontractor"` and `stock_entry.subcontracting_order = SCO.name`; - for each supplied row, creates a `Stock Entry Detail` with `s_warehouse` = RM warehouse/`reserve_warehouse`, **`t_warehouse = source_doc.supplier_warehouse`** (the company-owned warehouse representing material lying with the job worker), `subcontracted_item`/`main_item_code` = FG item, and **`sco_rm_detail` = the `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` row name** — the permanent link used for reconciliation; - caps transfer at `required_qty − total_supplied_qty` plus `Buying Settings.over_transfer_allowance`. - Submission/cancel logic lives in **`SendToSubcontractorStockEntry`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/subcontracting.py`), dispatched by purpose in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py` (purpose→service map ~line 200; `subcontract_data` dict with `order_field="subcontracting_order"`, `rm_detail_field="sco_rm_detail"` at 178–187): - `validate_subcontract_order` → `validate_subcontracting_order_for_bom` / `validate_subcontracting_order_for_transfer`, checking against `get_total_supplied_qty` / `get_total_returned_qty`; - `on_submit`/`on_cancel` → **`update_subcontract_order_supplied_items`** → `get_supplied_items` (214–249, aggregates `transfer_qty` of all submitted SEs per `sco_rm_detail`) → `_update_supplied_items_in_order` writes **`supplied_qty`, `returned_qty`, `total_supplied_qty` back onto the `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` rows** → `_update_reserved_qty_for_subcontracting` updates bins. - Stock effect: a plain two-leg transfer, so RM value simply relocates from the company store to the supplier warehouse. - Visibility: report `Subcontracted Raw Materials To Be Transferred` (`erpnext/buying/report/subcontracted_raw_materials_to_be_transferred/`). Excess material can be brought back via `get_materials_from_supplier` → `make_return_stock_entry_for_subcontract` / `add_items_in_ste` (controller, 1469–1557), powered by `SubcontractingController.get_available_materials`. ## 3. Finished goods receipt: `SubcontractingReceipt` - `make_subcontracting_receipt` → `get_mapped_subcontracting_receipt` (`erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_order/subcontracting_order.py`, 440–491): maps SCO → `Subcontracting Receipt` with pending qty, `subcontracting_order_item`/`bom` links, `process_loss_qty` from BOM `process_loss_percentage`, and copies the cost per-qty fields (`rm_cost_per_qty`, `service_cost_per_qty`, `additional_cost_per_qty`) from the order item. Class `SubcontractingReceipt` (`subcontracting_receipt.py`, 30–723) extends `SubcontractingController`. - Order tracking on submit: the `status_updater` in `__init__` (103–116) + `update_prevdoc_status` push `received_qty` into `Subcontracting Order Item.received_qty` and recompute `per_received` ("Partially Received"/"Completed" via `SubcontractingOrder.update_status`); returns extend it in `update_status_updater_args` (651–676). ## 4. Reconciling consumption against what was transferred - `SubcontractingController.validate` → `create_raw_materials_supplied_or_received("supplied_items")` builds the `Subcontracting Receipt Supplied Item` rows. Mode comes from `Buying Settings.backflush_raw_materials_of_subcontract_based_on`: - **"Material Transferred for Subcontract"**: `__prepare_supplied_or_received_items` (1039–1047) → **`get_available_materials`** (463–535) → `__get_transferred_items` (312–358) queries every submitted SE with `purpose="Send to Subcontractor"` (plus is_return "Material Transfer") joined to the SCOs, keyed by `(rm_item_code, main_item_code, subcontracting_order)` with serial/batch data from Serial-and-Batch Bundles; **`__update_consumed_materials`** (398–461) subtracts quantities already consumed by earlier Subcontracting Receipts (`__get_received_items`, `__get_consumed_items`). Then `__set_supplied_or_received_items` (932–976) allocates available qty per FG row (`__get_qty_based_on_material_transfer`) and `__add_supplied_or_received_item` sets **`consumed_qty`** + serial/batch bundle (`__set_serial_and_batch_bundle`, `set_rate_for_supplied_items`). - **"BOM"**: consumption is recomputed from the BOM (`_get_materials_from_bom`), manual rows wiped by `SubcontractingReceipt.reset_supplied_items` (362–374), and limits enforced by `validate_bom_required_qty` + `get_rm_wise_consumed_qty` (603–649) when `validate_consumed_qty` is on. - Feedback to the order: `SubcontractingController.set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` → `__update_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order` (1110–1142) writes `consumed_qty` back onto `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item`; `SubcontractingReceipt.set_available_qty_for_consumption` (460–494) shows `total_supplied_qty − consumed_qty` per row. ## 5. Cost roll-up and accounting on receipt - `SubcontractingController.set_valuation_rate_for_rm` (70–100): re-prices each supplied row at the supplier warehouse's live valuation via `get_incoming_rate` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py`) so consumption is valued at true current cost. - `SubcontractingReceipt.set_missing_values` (455–458): `calculate_additional_costs` (controller, 1243–1271) distributes extra charges into `additional_cost_per_qty`, then **`SubcontractingReceipt.calculate_items_qty_and_amount`** (496–562) performs the roll-up: `rm_supp_cost` = Σ consumed amounts per FG row → `rm_cost_per_qty`, adds `secondary_items_cost_per_qty` (co-product/scrap rows appended by `get_secondary_items`, 377–445, allocated by BOM `cost_allocation_per`), LCV per-qty, giving **`item.rate = rm_cost_per_qty + service_cost_per_qty + additional_cost_per_qty + lcv_cost_per_qty`**. - `SubcontractingReceipt.on_submit` (168–185): `validate_closed_subcontracting_order`, `validate_bom_required_qty`, `set_subcontracting_order_status`, `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order`, **`update_stock_ledger`** (controller 1181–1221: FG SLE into the accepted warehouse at the rolled-up rate with `recalculate_rate=1`; rejected-qty SLE; and `make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse` 1163–1179 issues consumed RM out of `supplier_warehouse`), then `make_gl_entries` + `repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `update_status`, `auto_create_purchase_receipt` (→ `mapper.py::make_purchase_receipt`), `update_job_card`. - **GL**: `SubcontractingReceipt.get_gl_entries` (703–708) → `SubcontractingReceiptGLComposer` (`services/gl_composer.py`): debits FG inventory with the SLE `stock_value_difference` (the rolled-up cost), credits the FG `expense_account` with `stock_value_diff − service_cost` (raw-material share), credits `service_expense_account` with the service charge, reclassifies consumed RM out of the supplier-warehouse inventory account when `rm_supp_cost` is set, books additional costs, and posts any `divisional_loss` to `stock_adjustment_account`; LCV entries via `_make_item_gl_entries_for_lcv`. **In one sentence:** the SCO's `Subcontracting Order Supplied Item` rows (built from the BOM) are linked into each "Send to Subcontractor" Stock Entry via `sco_rm_detail`; submitting those entries updates `supplied_qty/total_supplied_qty` on the order; the Subcontracting Receipt then backflushes `consumed_qty` from the transferred-not-yet-consumed pool keyed by `(rm_item_code, main_item_code, subcontracting_order)`, rolls `rm + service + additional + LCV` cost into the FG's incoming rate, books the inventory/expense GL split, and pushes `received_qty`/`per_received` back into the Subcontracting Order (and `subcontracted_qty` into the Purchase Order via `update_subcontracted_quantity_in_po`).

**Cost roll-up**: **`calculate_items_qty_and_amount()`** (SCR L496) sets `rm_supp_cost` = Σ(consumed_qty × rate) of the receipt's supplied rows, `rm_cost_per_qty = rm_supp_cost / received_qty`, adds `secondary_items_cost_per_qty`, `service_cost_per_qty` (from the SCO/PO service item), `additional_cost_per_qty` (from `calculate_additional_costs`, controller L1243) and `landed_cost_voucher_amount`, i.e. `rate = rm + service + additional + LCV` (with BOM `cost_allocation_per` applied). `get_supplied_items_cost(item_row_id)` (controller L1223) is the per-FG helper. - **Stock ledger**: `update_stock_ledger()` (controller L1181) → FG entries (+qty at `warehouse`/`rejected_warehouse`, `incoming_rate = item.rate`, `recalculate_rate = 1` so weighted-average revaluation happens) and RM consumption entries at the supplier warehouse via **`make_sl_entries_for_supplier_warehouse()`** (L1163, `actual_qty = −consumed_qty`). - Finally `update_status()` (SCR L678 → "Completed"/"Return"/"Return Issued") and `auto_create_purchase_receipt()` (L710, `make_purchase_receipt` in `erpnext/subcontracting/doctype/subcontracting_receipt/mapper.py`) when `Buying Settings.auto_create_purchase_receipt` is set — the supplier-billing document. **Legacy parallel path**: a subcontracted PO received directly through `Purchase Receipt` / `Purchase Invoice (update_stock)` uses the same controller — `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py` L385/L467 calls `set_consumed_qty_in_subcontract_order()`, with `purchase_order` as the order doctype, `po_detail` as `rm_detail_field`, and `Purchase Receipt Item Supplied` as the consumed-items table.

final answer
I've traced the full flow. Here's the complete answer. ## Overview Two files do almost all the work: - **`erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`** — class `LandedCostVoucher` (distribution + the retroactive repost driver `update_landed_cost`) - **`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`** (`update_valuation_rate`, `update_stock_ledger`), **`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`** (`make_gl_entries`, `make_gl_entries_on_cancel`, `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`, `repost_future_sle_and_gle`), and **`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`** (`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer`) — the PR-side recomputation. ## 1. Pulling receipt lines into the LCV - `LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` (whitelisted; wired to the "Get Items from Purchase Receipts" button in `landed_cost_voucher.js`) iterates the `purchase_receipts` child table and calls the module-level **`get_pr_items(pr)`** (same file). That query reads the `Purchase Receipt Item` child rows (joined to `Item`, filtered to stock/fixed-asset items) and appends one **`Landed Cost Item`** row per PR line, storing `item_code`, `qty`, `base_rate`/`base_amount`, `cost_center`, and — critically — the exact child row name in `purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item` for Stock Entries). This row-level link is what allows per-line redistribution and later matching. (The PR dashboard helper `make_lcv()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py` pre-fills an LCV from a single PR.) - The `taxes` table (`Landed Cost Taxes and Charges`) holds one row per freight/customs/duty charge with `expense_account` and `amount`. **`init_landed_taxes_and_totals`** (a helper class in `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py`) sets account currency/exchange rate and computes `base_amount`; `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` sums these into `total_taxes_and_charges`. ## 2. Redistributing charges across line items - **`LandedCostVoucher.set_applicable_charges_on_item()`**: if `distribute_charges_based_on` is `"Qty"` or `"Amount"` (scrubbed to `qty`/`amount`), it computes `total_item_cost` across all item rows and sets each row's `applicable_charges = item.qty_or_amount × (total_taxes_and_charges / total_item_cost)`. Any rounding remainder (`total_charges != total_taxes_and_charges`) is dumped onto the last item row. - If `"Distribute Manually"`, the user types `applicable_charges` per row; **`validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`** (called from `on_submit()`) verifies Σ `applicable_charges` equals `total_taxes_and_charges` to field precision, auto-adjusting the last row for rounding diff, otherwise throwing *"Total Applicable Charges in Purchase Receipt Items table must be same as Total Taxes and Charges"*. ## 3. Retroactive update of already-submitted Purchase Receipts `on_submit()` calls **`LandedCostVoucher.update_landed_cost()`**, which loops over every `purchase_receipts` row in two phases: **Phase A — recompute item values directly in the DB (no full doc.save):** 1. `validate_asset_qty_and_status()` blocks the LCV if submitted Assets already exist for the receipt (asset rates can't be changed this way). 2. Module-level **`set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`**: for each PR item row, it aggregates `SUM(applicable_charges)` across **all** submitted LCVs matching `receipt_document` + `purchase_receipt_item` and writes `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` (also backfills `cost_center` via `db_set`). 3. **`doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`** (`BuyingController.update_valuation_rate`) recomputes each item's valuation including the LCV amount: `valuation_rate = (base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom`. 4. Each child row is persisted with **`item.db_update()`** — deliberately avoiding a full `save()` so validations/status logic don't rerun. 5. `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` pushes the new `valuation_rate` into `Serial No.purchase_rate`. **Phase B — simulate cancel + resubmit of ledger effects (docstatus is toggled in memory only):** - With `doc.docstatus = 2`: `doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` posts **reversing (Outward) SLEs**; `doc.make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` (→ `make_reverse_gl_entries`) reverses the old GL entries. - With `doc.docstatus = 1`: `doc.make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` rebuilds Serial/Batch bundles, then `update_stock_ledger(...)` posts fresh **Inward SLEs with `incoming_rate = d.valuation_rate`** (now including landed cost). The `via_landed_cost_voucher` + `allow_negative_stock` flags propagate down to `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py::make_sl_entries/make_entry` and `erpnext/stock/serial_batch_bundle.py::update_batch_qty` to suppress negative-stock/serial validation during the repost. - **`doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** → `StockController.make_gl_entries` → `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries` → **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`): - The stock-account debit (`stock_value_diff`) comes from the freshly recomputed SLE via `get_stock_value_difference(doc.name, d.name, d.warehouse)` (purchase_receipt.py), so it now includes the landed cost. - **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries(item)`** consumes `doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` — the `StockController` wrapper around **`get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)`** in landed_cost_voucher.py, which rebuilds a `(item_code, receipt_item_row) → {expense_account: {amount, base_amount}}` map from every submitted LCV, re-spreading each tax row's `base_amount` by the same qty/amount basis (or `applicable_charges` for manual distribution), and credits each landed-cost expense account per item against Stock Received But Not Billed. - `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry()` books any gap between the doc-based valuation (which includes `landed_cost_voucher_amount`) and the actual stock value difference to the loss/PPV account; `make_expenses_added_to_stock_entries()` optionally books the "Expenses Added To Stock" pair (`BaseStockGLComposer.append_expenses_added_to_stock_pair` in `erpnext/stock/services/base_stock_gl_composer.py`). - **`doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle` → `create_repost_item_valuation_entry`/`create_item_wise_repost_entries` in stock_controller.py) queues **Repost Item Valuation** records so every *subsequent* stock movement (transfers, deliveries, manufacturing) and its GL entries is revalued against the new incoming rate — that's how the freight propagates into downstream COGS. Finally, `update_claimed_landed_cost()` marks the vendor Purchase Invoices with `claimed_landed_cost_amount` (and clears it on cancel). `on_cancel()` simply reruns the same `update_landed_cost()`: `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` now returns 0 for the cancelled LCV, so the landed cost is stripped from the items and everything is reposted back.

final answer
I now have the complete picture. Here's the full mechanism: # Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) — Distribution & Retroactive Posting ## 1. Distributing charges across receipt line items **Setup — pulling in the receipt items** - `LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py:58`), backed by `get_pr_items()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:426`), copies every stock/fixed-asset row of each receipt listed in the `purchase_receipts` child table (`Landed Cost Purchase Receipt`) into the `Landed Cost Item` child table. Each row stores `item_code`, `qty`, `amount` (base amount), `cost_center`, and the exact child-row name in `purchase_receipt_item` — this row-name link is what makes per-line redistribution possible later. - The `purchase_receipts` table accepts **multiple** receipts (Purchase Receipt, Purchase Invoice with Update Stock, Subcontracting Receipt, Stock Entry), each validated by `validate_receipt_documents()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:124`) to be submitted, same-company, etc. **The spread itself** — `distribute_charges_based_on` = `Qty`, `Amount`, or `Distribute Manually`: - Server-side: `LandedCostVoucher.set_applicable_charges_on_item()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:207`) computes, per item row: `applicable_charges = row[based_on] × total_taxes_and_charges ÷ Σ(row[based_on])`, with any rounding remainder dumped onto the last row. This mirrors the client-side `set_applicable_charges_for_item()` in `landed_cost_voucher.js:75`. - Manual mode is reconciled at submit by `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:237`): total `applicable_charges` must equal `total_taxes_and_charges` within field precision; sub-precision differences are pushed to the last row. - Charge rows live in `taxes` (`Landed Cost Taxes and Charges`: `expense_account`, `amount`, `exchange_rate`, `base_amount`). `init_landed_taxes_and_totals` (`erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py:1341`) resolves each account's currency/exchange rate and computes `base_amount = amount × exchange_rate`; `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:204`) sums the base amounts. ## 2. Retroactively updating already-submitted Purchase Receipts `on_submit()` → **`update_landed_cost()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:312`), which works in two phases over *each referenced, already-submitted receipt*: **Phase A — recompute item data directly in the DB (no docstatus change):** 1. `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:532`) — for each `Purchase Receipt Item` row, `SUM(applicable_charges)` over **all** submitted `Landed Cost Item` rows where `receipt_document = PR.name` and `purchase_receipt_item = row.name`. Result is written into `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount` (cumulative, so multiple LCVs against the same PR stack). It also backfills `cost_center`. 2. `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` → `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:414`), where the rate formula explicitly adds the LCV amount: `valuation_rate = (base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) ÷ qty_in_stock_uom` 3. Each item row is persisted via `item.db_update()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:329`) — this is how a submitted PR's rows are rewritten in place. 4. `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:395`) refreshes `Serial No.purchase_rate`; asset quantities are guarded by `validate_asset_qty_and_status()`. **Phase B — cancel-and-repost stock ledger + GL.** The PR is *not* actually cancelled; the LCV fakes both states: ```python doc.docstatus = 2 doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True) doc.make_gl_entries_on_cancel() doc.docstatus = 1 doc.make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True) doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True) doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True) doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True) ``` - **SLEs:** with `docstatus = 2`, `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` (`buying_controller.py:754`) builds reversal SLEs (`is_cancelled=1` via `StockLedgerService.get_sl_entries`, `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:80`) and `make_sl_entries` → `make_entry()` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:104/252`) cancels the old entries; `allow_negative_stock=True` and `via_landed_cost_voucher` suppress validations that would block the synthetic cancel. With `docstatus = 1`, fresh SLEs are inserted with **`incoming_rate = d.valuation_rate`** (`buying_controller.py:833`) — i.e., the new LCV-inclusive valuation. - **GLEs:** `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:281`) reverses the old entries via `make_reverse_gl_entries` (`erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`). Re-submission runs `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:478`) → `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py:23`), where: - `_make_item_gl_entries()` debits the warehouse account with the regenerated `stock_value_difference` (read back from the new SLEs by `get_stock_value_difference`, `purchase_receipt.py:544`) and credits Stock Received But Not Billed. - **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries()`** (`gl_composer.py:166`) is the LCV-specific GL: it consumes `doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` → `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:562`), which re-spreads each LCV tax row's `amount`/`base_amount` per (item_code, PR item row) per **LCV expense account** using the voucher's distribution basis. For each matched item row it **credits the freight/customs expense account against the stock account** — that's the accounting recognition of the landed cost, while the debit side has already been capitalized into inventory via the higher `incoming_rate`. - `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry()` (`gl_composer.py:233`) adds `landed_cost_voucher_amount` into the "valuation as per doc" so any residual lands on the divisional-loss account; for fixed assets, `doc.update_assets(d, d.valuation_rate)` revalues assets. - **Downstream ripple:** `repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` → `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle` (`stock_ledger_service.py:219`) → `create_repost_item_valuation_entry`/`create_item_wise_repost_entries` (`stock_controller.py`), which queue `Repost Item Valuation` records handled by `erpnext/stock/doctype/repost_item_valuation/repost_item_valuation.py` — recalculating FIFO/MA valuation and GL for every *subsequent* voucher touching the same item/warehouse, so deliveries and transfers issued before the LCV existed get re-valued too. **Cancellation symmetry:** `on_cancel()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:299`) reruns the same `update_landed_cost()`; since the LCV is now docstatus 2, `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` sums only docstatus-1 LCV items, so its charges drop out of `valuation_rate`, and the same fake-cancel/repost cycle removes both its SLE and GL effect. **Bonus:** `make_lcv()` (`purchase_receipt.py:570`) prefills an LCV from a Purchase Receipt via the dashboard shortcut; `has_landed_cost_amount()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:554`) gates whether LCV GL logic applies at all.

Here's the complete picture. # Overview The Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) never modifies a Purchase Receipt's status — it writes extra cost fields directly into the *already submitted* PR rows, recomputes valuation in memory, then fakes a cancel→resubmit cycle of the PR to regenerate Stock Ledger Entries (SLEs) and GL Entries. All the core logic lives in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`. ## 1. Pulling PR line items into the LCV (the redistribution basis) - `make_lcv(doctype, docname)` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:570` (the "Create Landed Cost Voucher" button) builds a draft LCV with a row in the `purchase_receipts` child table and calls `get_items_from_purchase_receipts()`. - `LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()` — `landed_cost_voucher.py:59` calls the module-level query `get_pr_items()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:426`), which joins `{Receipt Doc Type} Item` with `Item` and pulls **only stock items or fixed assets** (`is_stock_item=1 OR is_fixed_asset=1`), copying `qty`, `base_rate`/`base_amount`, `cost_center`, and storing the exact row link in `item.purchase_receipt_item` (or `stock_entry_item` for Stock Entry). - `validate()` (`:82`) runs `check_mandatory`, `validate_receipt_documents` (`:124` — receipt must be **docstatus 1**, same company; Purchase Invoices must have `update_stock`), `validate_line_items` (`:100` — each row must exist in the referenced receipt), and `init_landed_taxes_and_totals` (`erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py:1341` — sets currency/exchange rate and computes `amount`/`base_amount` per tax row). ## 2. Redistributing charges across items - `set_applicable_charges_on_item()` — `landed_cost_voucher.py:207`: when `distribute_charges_based_on` is **"Qty"** or **"Amount"**, `based_on_field = frappe.scrub(...)` → each item gets `applicable_charges = item.qty (or item.amount) × total_taxes_and_charges / Σ(item amounts)`; any rounding remainder is dumped onto the **last item** (`:233-235`). - `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()` — `landed_cost_voucher.py:237`: for **"Distribute Manually"**, it verifies the manually entered `applicable_charges` sum equals `total_taxes_and_charges` (within field precision, auto-adjusting the last row for rounding diff, otherwise `frappe.throw`). - `set_total_taxes_and_charges()` (`:204`) sums the `taxes` table (freight, customs duty, insurance — each row is an `expense_account` + amount). ## 3. Retroactive update of the submitted PR — `on_submit()` → `update_landed_cost()` `on_submit` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:294`) calls `validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`, `update_landed_cost()` (`:312`), and `update_claimed_landed_cost()` (`:303` — sets `claimed_landed_cost_amount` on vendor Purchase Invoices). `update_landed_cost()`, per receipt row, does two passes: **Pass 1 — write cost into the PR item rows:** 1. `frappe.get_doc(receipt_document_type, receipt_document)` loads the submitted PR. 2. `validate_asset_qty_and_status()` (`:357`) — all fixed-asset qty must be linked to draft Assets (not submitted). 3. `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)` (`:532`) — runs `Sum(applicable_charges)` + `Max(cost_center)` over **all submitted `Landed Cost Item` rows** where `receipt_document == doc.name` and `purchase_receipt_item == d.name`, writing the result into `d.landed_cost_voucher_amount` on each PR item (so multiple LCVs accumulate). Backfills `cost_center` via `db_set` if empty. 4. `doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)` — `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate()` in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:414`, which computes: `valuation_rate = (net_rate + item_tax_amount + flt(item.landed_cost_voucher_amount) + amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice) / qty_in_stock_uom` (`buying_controller.py:481-486`) — **this is where the freight/customs share enters the valuation rate**. 5. `item.db_update()` on every PR item (`:329-330`) — persists `landed_cost_voucher_amount` and the new valuation fields straight to the DB, bypassing save (the PR remains docstatus 1). 6. `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items()` (`:395`) — rewrites `Serial No.purchase_rate` to the new `valuation_rate`. **Pass 2 — the "fake cancel, then resubmit" repost (`:340-355`):** for each receipt doc, in memory: - `doc.docstatus = 2` → `doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` (`BuyingController.update_stock_ledger`, `buying_controller.py:754`) posts **reversal SLEs** (negative stock allowed so it can't fail), and `doc.make_gl_entries_on_cancel()` (`StockController.make_gl_entries_on_cancel`, `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:281`) — since `docstatus==2`, `StockController.make_gl_entries` (`:178`) calls `make_reverse_gl_entries`, cancelling the old GL postings. - `doc.docstatus = 1` → `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` rebuilds Serial/Batch Bundles, then `update_stock_ledger(...)` posts **fresh inward SLEs with `"incoming_rate": d.valuation_rate`** (`buying_controller.py:833`) — now LCV-inclusive. - `doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` regenerates GL entries (below), and `doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` → `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:219`) queues **`Repost Item Valuation`** for every subsequent stock/accounting voucher so downstream item costs (including future deliveries/sales of the same stock) recompute with the new valuation (`stock_controller.py:815,853` copy the flag onto the repost entries). ## 4. GL postings with LCV amounts `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries(inventory_account_map, via_landed_cost_voucher)` (`purchase_receipt.py:478`) → `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py:23`: - `landed_cost_entries = doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` (`gl_composer.py:302`) — `StockController.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries` (`stock_controller.py:267`) → `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:562`): from every submitted LCV against this PR, builds a map `(item_code, purchase_receipt_item) → {expense_account: {amount, base_amount}}`, re-splitting each tax row by the LCV's distribution basis (`qty`/`amount`, or `applicable_charges` when "Distribute Manually"). Gated by `has_landed_cost_amount(doc)` (`:554`). - Inside `_make_item_gl_entries` (`:39`): - `make_item_asset_inward_gl_entry` debits the warehouse/stock account with `stock_value_diff` — for **fixed assets** that's explicitly `base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount` (`:306`); for stock items it's `get_stock_value_difference(...)` from the new SLEs. - `make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry` credits *Stock Received But Not Billed* only with the original `base_net_amount`. - **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries`** (`:166-192`) — the key entry: credits each LCV `expense_account` (freight/customs) with the item's share, `against_account = stock_asset_account_name`. This balances the equation: Stock A/c Dr (incl. LCV) = SRNB Cr + valuation-tax credits + LCV expense-account credits. - `make_expenses_added_to_stock_entries` (`:194`) optionally books an "Expenses Included In Valuation" pair when `book_stock_expense` is enabled. - `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` (`:233`) includes `landed_cost_voucher_amount` in `valuation_amount_as_per_doc` when computing the divisional-loss entry. - For fixed assets, `doc.update_assets(d, d.valuation_rate)` (`purchase_receipt.py:499`) rewrites `Asset.purchase_amount`/`net_purchase_amount` (`:343-344`). ## 5. Cancellation and edge cases - `on_cancel` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:299`) reruns `update_landed_cost()`: `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` recomputes to the remaining (0) sum, `update_valuation_rate` drops the LCV component, and the same cancel/repost cycle reverts SLEs and GL entries; `update_claimed_landed_cost` resets the vendor invoice's `claimed_landed_cost_amount` to 0. - For internal transfers, `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:2540-2568`) reads the PR item's `landed_cost_voucher_amount` and adds `lcv_amount / |actual_qty|` to the transferred incoming rate. - The `via_landed_cost_voucher` flag threads through `make_sl_entries`, serial/bundle handling (`get_package_for_target_warehouse`, `buying_controller.py:895`), `Repost Item Valuation` creation, and the GL composer — it marks the operation as LCV-driven so, e.g., existing bundles are reused instead of recreated. **Summary of key files:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py` (distribution + retro-update orchestration), `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py` (`update_valuation_rate`, `update_stock_ledger`), `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py` (`make_gl_entries`, `make_gl_entries_on_cancel`, `repost_future_sle_and_gle`, `get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`), `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` (LCV GL entries), `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py` (`get_gl_entries`, `make_lcv`, `update_assets`), and `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py` (`init_landed_taxes_and_totals`).

Here's the full answer. # How a Landed Cost Voucher (LCV) works Everything lives in **`erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/landed_cost_voucher.py`** (class `LandedCostVoucher`), with the receipt-side plumbing in `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`, `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py`, and `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`. ## 1. Pulling receipt line items into the LCV - **`LandedCostVoucher.get_items_from_purchase_receipts()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:59`, whitelisted, wired to the "Get Items from Purchase Receipts" button via `landed_cost_voucher.js:47`) loops over the `purchase_receipts` child table (`LandedCostPurchaseReceipt` rows, which can also reference Purchase Invoice "Update Stock", Stock Entry, or Subcontracting Receipt) and calls the module-level query **`get_pr_items(purchase_receipt)`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:426`). - `get_pr_items` selects the referenced document's child rows (`Purchase Receipt Item`, `Stock Entry Detail`, etc.) **inner-joined with `tabItem` filtered to `is_stock_item = 1 OR is_fixed_asset = 1`**, and one `LandedCostItem` row is appended per line item, carrying `qty`, `rate`, `amount` (base), `cost_center`, and critically the row's identity: **`item.purchase_receipt_item = d.name`** (the PR item rowname) plus `receipt_document_type` / `receipt_document`. - **`validate()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:82`) enforces: `check_mandatory`, **`validate_receipt_documents`** (every referenced doc must be submitted — `docstatus == 1` — belong to the same company, and a Purchase Invoice must have `update_stock`; every item row must map to a listed receipt), **`validate_line_items`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:100`, the `purchase_receipt_item` row must still exist in that doc), and **`validate_expense_accounts`**; then `init_landed_taxes_and_totals(self)` (from `erpnext/controllers/taxes_and_totals.py`) and `set_total_taxes_and_charges`. ## 2. Redistributing the charges across line items - **`set_applicable_charges_on_item()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:207`) does the proportional split. If `distribute_charges_based_on` is `Qty` or `Amount` (not "Distribute Manually"), it scrubs that field, sums `total_item_cost` over all LCV item rows, and sets: `item.applicable_charges = item[based_on_field] × total_taxes_and_charges / total_item_cost` Rounding remainder is dumped on the **last** item row. If "Distribute Manually", the user types `applicable_charges` per row. - On submit, **`validate_applicable_charges_for_item()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:237`) re-verifies that `sum(applicable_charges)` equals `total_taxes_and_charges` to field precision, adjusting a tiny rounding diff on the last row and throwing otherwise. - The same distribution ratio is later re-derived per tax account by **`get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries(doc)`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:562`, reached via `StockController.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries`, `stock_controller.py:267`): it finds all *submitted* `Landed Cost Purchase Receipt` rows pointing at the doc, loads each LCV, and builds `{(item_code, purchase_receipt_item): {expense_account: {amount, base_amount}}}`, splitting each `taxes.expense_account` row's amount across items by the same `distribute_charges_based_on` basis (falling back to `applicable_charges` itself for manual distribution). ## 3. Retroactively updating the already-submitted Purchase Receipt **`LandedCostVoucher.on_submit()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:294`) calls **`update_landed_cost()`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:312`) — `on_cancel()` calls the same function to roll back, since `set_landed_cost_voucher_amount` recomputes from *currently submitted* LCVs. Per referenced receipt document, in two phases: **Phase A — recompute valuation on the receipt items (lines 313–338):** 1. `validate_asset_qty_and_status` — fixed-asset items must have matching `Asset` records. 2. Module-level **`set_landed_cost_voucher_amount(doc)`** (`landed_cost_voucher.py:532`): for each receipt item row, it sums `applicable_charges` over the `Landed Cost Item` table of all submitted LCVs where `receipt_document == doc.name AND purchase_receipt_item == d.name`, and writes it into **`d.landed_cost_voucher_amount`** (also `db_set`s `cost_center` if blank). This same helper is invoked during normal `BuyingController.validate()` (`buying_controller.py:38,66`), so any later amend/validate of the PR also sees LCV charges. 3. **`doc.update_valuation_rate(reset_outgoing_rate=False)`** (`buying_controller.py:414`) recomputes each item's valuation, where the LCV charge is an explicit term: `valuation_rate = (base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount + amount_difference) / qty_in_stock_uom` 4. Each item row is persisted with a raw **`item.db_update()`** (no full save/revalidation of a submitted doc). 5. `update_rate_in_serial_no_for_non_asset_items` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:395`) pushes the new `valuation_rate` into `Serial No.purchase_rate`. **Phase B — cancel-and-repost the submitted voucher's ledgers (lines 340–355):** for each receipt doc: - **Simulated cancellation** (`doc.docstatus = 2`): `doc.update_stock_ledger(allow_negative_stock=True, via_landed_cost_voucher=True)` → `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` (`buying_controller.py:754`) builds reversal SLEs, then **`doc.make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`** (`StockController`, `stock_controller.py`) reverses the PR's existing GL entries. - **Simulated resubmission** (`doc.docstatus = 1`): `make_bundle_using_old_serial_batch_fields(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`, `update_stock_ledger(...)` again — now emitting SLEs whose `incoming_rate = d.valuation_rate` (`buying_controller.py:833`) with the *new, charge-inclusive* rate — then **`doc.make_gl_entries(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`StockController.make_gl_entries`, `stock_controller.py:178`, which calls `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries(inventory_account_map, via_landed_cost_voucher)` at `purchase_receipt.py:478`). - Finally **`doc.repost_future_sle_and_gle(via_landed_cost_voucher=True)`** (`stock_controller.py:360` → `StockLedgerService.repost_future_sle_and_gle`) queues `Repost Item Valuation` work so all *subsequent* SLEs/GL entries (transfers, deliveries, later receipts of the same item) are re-valued and re-posted. The `via_landed_cost_voucher` flag threads into `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`: `make_sl_entries` (`stock_ledger.py:104`) → `repost_current_voucher` (`stock_ledger.py:172`) **skips re-posting the cancelled voucher's own SLEs** (`if not (args.get("is_cancelled") and via_landed_cost_voucher)`, line 177) while still updating future bins, and negative-stock validation is bypassed for serialized items during the LCV repost (`stock_ledger.py:1022`) — all with `allow_negative_stock=True` so a historical valuation change can't fail on interim negative stock. ## 4. GL postings for the LCV charge on the re-posted PR In **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`), `compose()` (`:23`) calls `_make_item_gl_entries` then `_make_tax_gl_entries`: - Line 302: `landed_cost_entries = doc.get_item_account_wise_lcv_entries()` is loaded per item. - **Debit side**: `make_item_asset_inward_gl_entry` debits the Stock/Asset (warehouse) account with `stock_value_diff = get_stock_value_difference(doc.name, d.name, d.warehouse)` (`:309`) — the stock ledger's recomputed incoming value, which now includes the LCV charge; for **fixed assets** it is explicitly `base_net_amount + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount` (`:306`). `make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry` still credits Stock Received But Not Billed only by `base_net_amount`. - **`make_landed_cost_gl_entries`** (`:166`): the balancing piece — for each `(item_code, pr_item_row)` it **credits each LCV `expense_account`** (customs/freight accounts from the LCV's `taxes` table) with that item's `amount`/`base_amount` share, against the stock account. So the extra capitalized value lands on the stock asset account with a corresponding credit to the landed-cost expense account rather than SRNB. - `make_expenses_added_to_stock_entries` (`:194`) optionally books the `landed_cost_voucher_amount` through the "book stock expense" pair, and `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` (`:233`) absorbs any residual between doc valuation (which includes `item.landed_cost_voucher_amount`) and the booked `stock_value_diff`. - Fixed assets additionally get `doc.update_assets(d, d.valuation_rate)` (`:344`) so gross asset value rises. - `_make_tax_gl_entries` (`:394`) handles only the PR's *own* valuation-category tax rows (`item_tax_amount`), separate from LCV charges. **Extra bookkeeping:** `update_claimed_landed_cost()` (`landed_cost_voucher.py:303`) sets `claimed_landed_cost_amount` on vendor Purchase Invoices (used by `get_vendor_invoice_query`, `:499`, to show remaining "unclaimed" service-invoice amounts that can be capitalized later). Behavioral examples are covered in `erpnext/stock/doctype/landed_cost_voucher/test_landed_cost_voucher.py` and `test_purchase_receipt.py` (e.g. the `via_landed_cost_voucher: 0` Repost Item Valuation assertions at lines 3747/3886/5631).
