final answer
I now have the complete trace. Here's the full picture: ## The holding spot: "Stock Received But Not Billed" (SRBNB) Between goods receipt and supplier bill, ERPNext parks the value in the **company default account `stock_received_but_not_billed`** — a Current Liability account of Account Type "Stock Received But Not Billed" (set on the Company; fetched via `doc.get_company_default("stock_received_but_not_billed")`). Fixed assets use the parallel `asset_received_but_not_billed`. It's the GR/IR-style provision: goods are in the warehouse, but no supplier payable exists yet. ## Receipt side — parking the value 1. `PurchaseReceipt.on_submit` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:363-383`) runs `update_stock_ledger()` then `self.make_gl_entries()`. 2. `make_gl_entries` is inherited from `StockController.make_gl_entries` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:178-205`): with perpetual inventory on, it builds `inventory_account_map` (warehouse → inventory account) and calls the shared `make_gl_entries()` from `erpnext/accounts/general_ledger.py`. 3. `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries` (`purchase_receipt.py:478-483`) delegates to `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`, which calls `_make_item_gl_entries()`. Per item, for stock/asset items: - **`make_item_asset_inward_gl_entry`** (gl_composer.py:57-72): **Dr** the warehouse's inventory account for `stock_value_diff` (actual stock value from the ledger via `get_stock_value_difference`, `purchase_receipt.py:544-555`). - **`make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry`** (gl_composer.py:74-164): **Cr** `stock_asset_rbnb` — the SRBNB company default — for `item.base_net_amount` (adjusted for internal transfers / rejected qty / landed cost). - Supporting entries: `make_landed_cost_gl_entries` (charges capitalized into stock), `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` (price variance → Purchase Price Variance account for Standard Cost items, via `get_divisional_loss_account`), `_make_tax_gl_entries` (credits valuation-tax accounts capitalized into stock). **Journal at receipt:** `Dr Stock In Hand / Cr Stock Received But Not Billed`. Inventory is capitalized, a liability is provisioned — **no Creditors entry, no P&L expense**. (Non-stock services have an analogous parking via `ProvisionalAccountingService.add_provisional_gl_entry` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/provisional_accounting.py`: Dr expense / Cr *Default Provisional Account*.) ## Billing side — moving the value out 1. **Validate (this is the crux):** `PurchaseInvoice.validate` (`purchase_invoice.py:288-297`) calls `ExpenseAccountService.set_expense_account(for_validate=True)` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/expense_account.py:20-158`. For stock items it **forces `item.expense_account` to the SRBNB account**: - If `item.purchase_receipt` is linked, it queries the GL Entry table (`negative_expense_booked_in_pr`) to confirm SRBNB was actually credited on that receipt, then sets the expense head to SRBNB (msgprint "Expense Head Changed" if it differed). - If **no** PR exists yet (bill created before receipt), it also forces SRBNB, so the same clearing logic works when the receipt arrives later. - `set_against_expense_account()` (expense_account.py:164-171) then collects the expense heads into `doc.against_expense_account`. 2. **On submit:** `PurchaseInvoice.on_submit` (`purchase_invoice.py:607-652`) updates billing status via `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr` — which (when "set landed cost based on PI rate" is on) computes and writes `amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice` back onto the PR rows (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py:258`) — then calls `self.make_gl_entries()` (purchase_invoice.py:671-689) → `get_gl_entries()` → `PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer.compose()` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`. 3. In `compose()`: - **`make_supplier_gl_entry`** (gl_composer.py:80-127): **Cr** `doc.credit_to` (Creditors) for the grand total, "against" `doc.against_expense_account` (= SRBNB). - **`make_item_gl_entries`** (gl_composer.py:129+): since `update_stock` is 0 for a bill-against-receipt, it takes the else-branch (lines 319-350, explicitly commented: *"the linked Purchase Receipt already booked the stock... Here we only clear 'Stock Received But Not Billed' at the full billed amount against the supplier"*): **Dr** `item.expense_account` — i.e. **SRBNB** — against `doc.supplier` for the billed amount. - Edge cases: if the invoice's exchange rate differs from the receipt's, extra SRBNB debit + `exchange_gain_loss_account` entries (lines 352-393); if the PR did *not* capitalize a valuation tax (`negative_expense_booked_in_pr` check, lines 395-439), SRBNB is also debited for `item_tax_amount`, accumulating `doc.negative_expense_to_be_booked` which `make_tax_gl_entries` (line 605+) later credits to the tax accounts. **Journal at bill:** `Dr Stock Received But Not Billed / Cr Creditors` — the debit lands exactly on the liability the receipt credited, cancelling the provision, and the *real* payable appears against the supplier. The asset stays in the stock account; no P&L expense is hit for stock items (value remains capitalized until issue/sale). ## Rate-difference reconciliation If the billed rate differs from the receipt rate: `BillingStatusService` writes `amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice` on the PR item; on repost, `make_amount_difference_entry` (gl_composer.py:202-216) posts "Adjustment based on Purchase Invoice rate" to SRBNB, and `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` includes it in the variance calc; `PurchaseReceipt.before_cancel` clears it via `remove_amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice` (`purchase_receipt.py:470-476`). (Note: if a Purchase Invoice is submitted with **Update Stock** checked — no separate receipt — the flow bypasses SRBNB entirely: the debit goes straight to the warehouse account via `make_stock_adjustment_entry` in the same composer.)

I now have the full picture across both sides. Here is the trace. ## The holding spot: "Stock Received But Not Billed" (the GR/IR account) ERPNext parks the value of received-but-unbilled goods in the **Stock Received But Not Billed (SRBNB)** liability account — the classic GR/IR clearing account. In the standard chart of accounts it lives under **Current Liabilities → Stock Liabilities** with `account_type: "Stock Received But Not Billed"` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/account/chart_of_accounts/verified/standard_chart_of_accounts.py:165`), and every Company gets it as a default via `stock_received_but_not_billed` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.py:704`, `create_default_accounts`). Code always fetches it with `doc.get_company_default("stock_received_but_not_billed")`. For fixed assets the parallel account is **Asset Received But Not Billed**. ## Receipt side — Purchase Receipt submit Chain: `PurchaseReceipt.on_submit()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:363`) → `make_gl_entries()` (line 383, inherited from `StockController`) → `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries()` (lines 478–483) → **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer.compose()`** in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py` → `_make_item_gl_entries()`. Per item (when perpetual inventory is enabled and there's a valuation rate): 1. `stock_asset_rbnb = doc.get_company_default("stock_received_but_not_billed")` (lines 297–301; `asset_received_but_not_billed` if `d.is_fixed_asset`). 2. **`make_item_asset_inward_gl_entry()`** (line 57) — **Debit** the warehouse's stock/asset account with `stock_value_diff`, which comes from the Stock Ledger via `get_stock_value_difference(doc.name, d.name, d.warehouse)`; `against_account` is the SRBNB account. 3. **`make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry()`** (line 74) — **Credit** the SRBNB account by the item's `base_net_amount` (posted as a negative debit, against the stock account). Also `make_amount_difference_entry()` (line 202) can re-touch SRBNB to absorb rate differences vs. an already-billed Purchase Invoice, and `_make_tax_gl_entries()` credits valuation-tax accounts against these debits. **Net books at receipt:** `Dr Stock/Inventory account / Cr Stock Received But Not Billed`. The stock asset is recognized, but *no supplier payable exists yet* — the value is parked in SRBNB, a liability owed to "nobody in particular" until the bill arrives. ## Billing side — Purchase Invoice submit Two things must happen: the item's expense account is pointed *at* SRBNB, and the composer posts a debit there. **Step 1 — retarget the expense account.** During `PurchaseInvoice.validate()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/purchase_invoice.py:257`, lines 288–291), **`ExpenseAccountService.set_expense_account()`** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/expense_account.py:20`) runs: - For stock items under perpetual inventory (lines 41–102): if the row has `item.purchase_receipt`, it checks whether SRBNB was actually credited in that PR (a `GL Entry` lookup against the PR, lines 56–67) and, if so, forces `item.expense_account = stock_not_billed_account` (line 82) — showing an "Expense Head Changed" message if validation had something else. If **no PR exists yet** (bill received before goods), it assigns SRBNB anyway so the later PR can reverse it (lines 83–102). The same default is injected at row level by `erpnext/stock/get_item_details.py:575–584` (`expense_account_field = "stock_received_but_not_billed"` for Purchase Receipt, or Purchase Invoice with `update_stock`). **Step 2 — compose the clearing entries.** `PurchaseInvoice.make_gl_entries()` (purchase_invoice.py:671) → `PurchaseInvoice.get_gl_entries()` (703–708) → **`PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer.compose()`** in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`: - `compose()` sets `doc.stock_received_but_not_billed = doc.get_company_default(...)` when perpetual inventory is on (lines 25–28). - **`make_supplier_gl_entry()`** (line 80) — **Credit** the supplier's `credit_to` (payable) account for the grand total, `against_expense_account` set by `ExpenseAccountService.set_against_expense_account()`. - **`make_item_gl_entries()`** (line 129) — for the normal billing-only invoice (no `update_stock`), each item lands in the `else` branch (lines 319–350): **Debit** `item.expense_account` (= SRBNB) against the supplier. The comment spells it out: *"the linked Purchase Receipt already booked the stock (at standard) and the Purchase Price Variance. Here we only clear 'Stock Received But Not Billed' at the full billed amount against the supplier."* - **Tax symmetry:** for stock items with `item_tax_amount`, lines 395–439 ("Post reverse entry for Stock-Received-But-Not-Billed if booked in Purchase Receipt") check the PR's GL entries for the valuation-tax accounts; any tax *not* already credited at receipt is **debited to SRBNB** and accumulated into `doc.negative_expense_to_be_booked`, which `make_tax_gl_entries()` (lines 650–680) then re-credits against the tax accounts. **Net books at billing:** `Dr Stock Received But Not Billed / Cr Creditors`. The debit exactly cancels the credit parked at receipt — SRBNB returns to zero, and the obligation moves from the suspense GR/IR account to the named supplier payable. (Cancellation reverses both sides via `make_gl_entries_on_cancel` / `make_reverse_gl_entries`.) ## The simultaneous-receipt variant When the Purchase Invoice has **`update_stock` checked** (goods arrive with the bill, no separate PR), `set_expense_account` takes the branch at lines 51–54 and sets `item.expense_account` to the warehouse's **inventory account** instead. Then `make_item_gl_entries` debits that inventory account directly against the supplier (`warehouse_debit_amount` from `make_stock_adjustment_entry`, lines 535–603, reconciled to the SLE's `stock_value_difference`) — goods and bill are the same event, so there is nothing to park and no SRBNB intermediate. ## One-line summary `Dr Stock / Cr Stock Received But Not Billed` at `PurchaseReceiptGLComposer._make_item_gl_entries` (receipt), then `ExpenseAccountService.set_expense_account` swaps the PI item's expense account to SRBNB so `PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer.make_item_gl_entries` posts `Dr SRBNB / Cr Creditors` (billing) — moving the held value out of the GR/IR holding account onto the supplier's ledger.

I have the complete picture across both sides. Here's the full trace. ## The holding spot: "Received But Not Billed" (RBNB) liability accounts ERPNext parks the value of received-but-unbilled goods in two interim liability accounts defined as Company defaults (`erpnext/setup/doctype/company/company.json`): - **`Stock Received But Not Billed`** (field `stock_received_but_not_billed`) — for stock items - **`Asset Received But Not Billed`** (field `asset_received_but_not_billed`) — for fixed assets Fetching happens via `doc.get_company_default("stock_received_but_not_billed" | "asset_received_but_not_billed")`. ## Receipt side — Parking the value (Purchase Receipt) 1. `PurchaseReceipt.on_submit` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:363`) calls `self.make_gl_entries()` (line 383) — inherited from `StockController.make_gl_entries` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:178`), which calls back into the doc's `get_gl_entries`. 2. `PurchaseReceipt.get_gl_entries` (purchase_receipt.py:478) delegates to **`PurchaseReceiptGLComposer(self).compose(...)`** in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py`. 3. `compose` → `_make_item_gl_entries` (gl_composer.py:39). Per item: - **Account selection** (lines 297–301): `stock_asset_rbnb = get_company_default("asset_received_but_not_billed")` if `d.is_fixed_asset`, else `get_company_default("stock_received_but_not_billed")`. - **`make_item_asset_inward_gl_entry`** (line 57): **DEBIT** the warehouse inventory account (value from `get_stock_value_difference`, purchase_receipt.py) or, for assets, `d.expense_account`, by the received value. - **`make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry`** (line 74): **CREDIT** the RBNB account by `item.base_net_amount`. Net effect at receipt: **Dr Stock/Asset : Cr Stock/Asset Received But Not Billed**. The value sits on the balance sheet with no supplier payable, because no bill exists yet. ## Billing side — Draining the holding spot (Purchase Invoice) 1. **Account forcing at validate time** — `PurchaseInvoice.validate` (purchase_invoice.py:257, line 288) runs `ExpenseAccountService(self).set_expense_account(for_validate=True)` from `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/expense_account.py`: - Stock items (lines 41–102): it queries `GL Entry` for the linked PR checking whether `stock_received_but_not_billed` was credited there (lines 57–65); if so, it **forces `item.expense_account = stock_not_billed_account`** (line 82) — the invoice's "expense" is the holding account itself, not a P&L account. Same logic if the invoice is made before the receipt (line 102). - Fixed assets with `pr_detail` (lines 103–156): fetches the `asset_received_but_not_billed` default (lines 121–124), checks the PR's GL for it (line 127), and sets `expense_account` to ARBNB (line 137); otherwise falls back to CWIP/Fixed Asset account. 2. **GL composition at submit** — `PurchaseInvoice.make_gl_entries` (purchase_invoice.py:671) → **`PurchaseInvoiceGLComposer(self).compose(...)`** in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/gl_composer.py`: - `make_supplier_gl_entry` (line 80) → `add_supplier_gl_entry` (line 94): **CREDIT `doc.credit_to`** (real supplier payable) for the grand total, against `doc.against_expense_account` (the RBNB accounts, collected by `ExpenseAccountService.set_against_expense_account`). - `make_item_gl_entries` (line 129): when `update_stock` is off (the invoice pulls from a PR via `purchase_receipt`/`pr_detail`), the else-branch (lines 319–350) **DEBITS `item.expense_account`** — i.e., SRBNB/ARBNB — against the supplier. The comment (lines 332–336) states it explicitly: *"the linked Purchase Receipt already booked the stock … Here we only clear 'Stock Received But Not Billed' at the full billed amount against the supplier."* - Valuation taxes: lines 395–439 post a reverse **debit to SRBNB** for `item.item_tax_amount` when the PR didn't already book the valuation tax ("Post reverse entry for Stock-Received-But-Not-Billed if booked in Purchase Receipt"). - Exchange-rate drift between PR and PI: lines 352–393 route the discrepancy through `exchange_gain_loss_account`, mirrored on the PR side (gl_composer.py:126–162). Net effect at billing: **Dr Stock Received But Not Billed : Cr Credit To (Accounts Payable)**. The value moves out of the interim liability into the genuine payable; the stock/asset debit is untouched, so no expense is double-booked. ## Supporting mechanics - **True-up at receipt**: `make_amount_difference_entry` (PR gl_composer.py:202) credits/debits RBNB by `amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice` so the parked value matches the eventual bill rate; `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` (line 233) absorbs purchase-price variance. - **Status linkage**: on PI submit, `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/billing_status.py` → `update_billing_status_in_pr` and `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py` → `update_billing_status` / `update_billing_percentage` set `billed_amt`/`per_billed` on PR items; `PurchaseReceipt.on_submit` flips the PR to "Completed" at 100% billed (purchase_receipt.py:372–375). - **Symmetric case (bill first)**: the invoice debits SRBNB against the supplier; when the PR is later received, `make_stock_received_but_not_billed_entry` credits SRBNB, netting the holding account to zero with the warehouse account carrying the value.

## Answer The check is a **server-side validation in the Pricing Rule doctype controller**, triggered automatically on every insert/save. ### Where it lives **File:** `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/pricing_rule.py` 1. **`PricingRule.validate()`** (line 130) — the standard Frappe document validation hook, which calls `self.validate_duplicate_apply_on()`. 2. **`PricingRule.validate_duplicate_apply_on()`** (lines 148–160) — since `apply_on != "Transaction"`, it resolves the relevant child table via the module-level mapping `apply_on_dict = {"Item Code": "items", "Item Group": "item_groups", "Brand": "brands"}` (line 15). With `apply_on = "Item Code"` it collects the `item_code` values from the `items` child table (`PricingRuleItemCode` rows) and: - First throws if the same item code is listed twice: `"Duplicate {0} found in the table"` (lines 155–157). Note this check alone does **not** catch the template/variant case, because a template and its variant are two distinct item codes. - Then, specifically for `apply_on == "Item Code"`, calls `self.validate_template_with_variant(values)` (lines 159–160). 3. **`PricingRule.validate_template_with_variant(item_codes)`** (lines 162–175) — this is the check that detects the conflicting configuration. It runs a single query: ```python frappe.get_all( "Item", filters={"name": ("in", item_codes), "variant_of": ("in", item_codes)}, fields=["name", "variant_of"], ) ``` **What it checks:** it looks for any Item row where both (a) the item's own name is in the rule's item list and (b) the item's `variant_of` (the link to its template) is *also* in the rule's item list. In other words, a self-referential "in-list × in-list" filter that matches only when a variant and its own template coexist in the same rule. Because the query conditions share the same list, a variant whose template is *not* in the rule won't match, and neither will unrelated items. If any row is returned, it throws a `frappe.ValidationError` (via `frappe.throw`): > **"Variant {0} and its template {1} cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule"** with the variant name and template name bolded, e.g. "Variant **Test Variant PRT** and its template **_Test Variant Item** cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule". This aborts the save/insert. ### What is *not* covered - There is **no client-side counterpart** — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/pricing_rule.js` contains no variant/duplicate checks; the guard runs only at save time on the server. - The check only applies to the "Item Code" apply-on child table. If the template/variant happen to be covered indirectly via "Item Group" or "Brand" apply-on rules, no such conflict check exists (variants inherit the template's item group/brand, but `validate_template_with_variant` is only invoked for the Item Code case). ### Test confirming the behavior `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/test_pricing_rule.py`, **`test_pricing_rule_with_template_and_its_variant`** (lines 336–359): it creates the variant `Test Variant PRT` with `variant_of = "_Test Variant Item"`, builds a Pricing Rule with `apply_on = "Item Code"` whose `items` table contains both `_Test Variant Item` (template) and `Test Variant PRT` (its variant), and asserts `self.assertRaises(frappe.ValidationError, rule.insert)` — i.e., the insert is rejected with exactly the validation described above.

## Answer Yes — there is an explicit save-time validation that catches exactly this case, and it rejects the document with a `frappe.ValidationError`. ### Where it runs `PricingRule.validate()` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/pricing_rule.py` (line 130) runs on every insert/save (Frappe calls `validate` during save and submit). Its second step is `self.validate_duplicate_apply_on()` (line 132). ### The two-stage check: `validate_duplicate_apply_on` (lines 148–160) 1. **Table/field resolution** — it maps `apply_on` to the child table via the module-level dict (line 15): ```python apply_on_dict = {"Item Code": "items", "Item Group": "item_groups", "Brand": "brands"} ``` For `apply_on == "Item Code"` this is the `items` child table (`Pricing Rule Item Code` rows), and the field is `frappe.scrub("Item Code")` → `item_code`. (For `apply_on == "Transaction"` it returns early — no check.) 2. **Literal-duplicate check first** (lines 155–157): it collects all non-empty `item_code` values from the rows and, if `len(values) != len(set(values))`, throws `"Duplicate Item Code found in the table"`. 3. **Template-vs-variant check** (lines 159–160): because `apply_on == "Item Code"`, it then calls `self.validate_template_with_variant(values)`. ### What `validate_template_with_variant` specifically checks (lines 162–175) It runs **one database query** against the `Item` doctype with a *double-membership* filter: ```python variants = frappe.get_all( "Item", filters={"name": ("in", item_codes), "variant_of": ("in", item_codes)}, fields=["name", "variant_of"], ) ``` This asks: *is there any Item whose own `name` is in the rule's item list **and** whose `variant_of` (its template parent) is also in that same list?* In other words, it looks for a (template, its direct variant) pair both present in the child rows. If the query returns any row, it throws: ``` Variant {variant.name} and its template {variant.variant_of} cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule ``` which aborts the save. Note the check relies on the `variant_of` link field on Item, so it catches the template and **its direct variants**; it doesn't apply to Item Group/Brand/Transaction rules. ### Confirmation by test `test_pricing_rule_with_template_and_its_variant` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/test_pricing_rule.py` (line 336) builds exactly your scenario — appends `_Test Variant Item` (template) and `Test Variant PRT` (a variant with `variant_of = "_Test Variant Item"`) to the same rule's `items` table with `apply_on = "Item Code"` — and asserts `self.assertRaises(frappe.ValidationError, rule.insert)`. ### Why this guard exists (apply-time context) At matching time, `_get_pricing_rules` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/utils.py` (lines 121–126) already expands a variant transaction line to also match its template row: ```python if args.variant_of: item_variant_condition = f" or {child_doc}.item_code=%(variant_of)s " ``` So a template row in a rule implicitly covers all of its variants. Listing template + variant explicitly would make one rule match the same line ambiguously (potentially multiple child rows hitting the same transaction item), which is precisely the conflicting configuration this validation prevents at save time. There is no client-side (JS) equivalent — the enforcement is purely server-side in `validate`.

## Answer Yes — a save-time validation catches exactly this case, and it lives entirely in the parent Pricing Rule controller (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/pricing_rule.py`). ### The validation chain at save time `PricingRule.validate()` (line 130) runs on every save and calls **`validate_duplicate_apply_on()`** (line 148): ```python def validate_duplicate_apply_on(self): if self.apply_on != "Transaction": apply_on_table = apply_on_dict.get(self.apply_on) # "Item Code" -> "items" ... apply_on_field = frappe.scrub(self.apply_on) # "item_code" values = [d.get(apply_on_field) for d in self.get(apply_on_table) if d.get(apply_on_field)] if len(values) != len(set(values)): frappe.throw(_("Duplicate {0} found in the table").format(self.apply_on)) if self.apply_on == "Item Code": self.validate_template_with_variant(values) # line 160 ``` Two checks happen here: 1. **Exact-duplicate check**: collects every `item_code` from the `items` child table (rows of the `PricingRuleItemCode` child doctype) and throws `"Duplicate Item Code found in the table"` if any value repeats. This alone would *not* catch a template + its variant, since they are different item codes. 2. **Template-vs-variant check** (only for `apply_on == "Item Code"`): calls `validate_template_with_variant(values)`. ### What `validate_template_with_variant()` specifically checks (lines 162–175) ```python def validate_template_with_variant(self, item_codes): # throws if a template and its variant both exist in one rule variants = frappe.get_all( "Item", filters={"name": ("in", item_codes), "variant_of": ("in", item_codes)}, fields=["name", "variant_of"], ) if variants: variant = variants[0] frappe.throw( _("Variant {0} and its template {1} cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule").format( frappe.bold(variant.name), frappe.bold(variant.variant_of) ) ) ``` The detection mechanism is a single query against the **Item** doctype using the `variant_of` field (the Link from a variant item back to its template item): it looks for any item whose **own name is in the rule's item list** *and* whose **template (`variant_of`) is also in that same list**. If the intersection is non-empty, `frappe.throw` raises a `ValidationError` with the message **"Variant X and its template Y cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule"** (both names bolded), which aborts the save. ### Scope / boundaries of the check - It's purely **intra-rule**: both SQL filters use the same `item_codes` list built from this one rule's `items` table, so a template in Rule A and its variant in Rule B is perfectly allowed. Only coexistence within one rule is rejected. - A variant alone (template not in the list) or a template alone passes fine — the `variant_of ("in", item_codes)` condition fails unless the template is also listed. - The same check does **not** exist for "Item Group" or "Brand" apply-on modes (it's gated on `apply_on == "Item Code"`), and it's skipped entirely for `apply_on == "Transaction"`. - The child doctype `PricingRuleItemCode` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule_item_code/pricing_rule_item_code.py`) is a plain pass-through Document (just `item_code` and `uom` Link fields, class body is `pass`) — all validation is centralized in the parent controller. - Notably, this snapshot has no dedicated test asserting this message; it appears only in the controller and in locale `.po` translation files (e.g., `erpnext/locale/main.pot` line 60680).

## Answer Yes — there is an explicit save-time validation for exactly this case, and it lives in the Pricing Rule doctype controller. ### The call chain at save time **`PricingRule.validate()`** — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/pricing_rule/pricing_rule.py:130` — runs (among others) `validate_duplicate_apply_on()` (line 132), which contains two layered checks: **1. `validate_duplicate_apply_on()` (lines 148–160)** Since `apply_on` is `"Item Code"` (not `"Transaction"`), it maps the apply-on value to the child table via the module-level dict at line 15: ```python apply_on_dict = {"Item Code": "items", "Item Group": "item_groups", "Brand": "brands"} ``` - `apply_on_field = frappe.scrub("Item Code")` → `"item_code"` - It collects `values = [d.get("item_code") for d in self.get("items") if d.get("item_code")]` — i.e., every item code in the rule's `items` child table (rows of doctype **`PricingRuleItemCode`**). - **Duplicate check (lines 156–157):** `if len(values) != len(set(values))` → throws `"Duplicate Item Code found in the table"`. This only catches the *same* item listed twice — it would **not** catch a template + its variant, since those are two different item codes. **2. `validate_template_with_variant(values)` (lines 159–160, 162–175)** — this is the check that catches your scenario, and it runs **only when `apply_on == "Item Code"`** (not for Item Group or Brand): ```python def validate_template_with_variant(self, item_codes): # throws if a template and its variant both exist in one rule variants = frappe.get_all( "Item", filters={"name": ("in", item_codes), "variant_of": ("in", item_codes)}, fields=["name", "variant_of"], ) if variants: variant = variants[0] frappe.throw( _("Variant {0} and its template {1} cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule").format( frappe.bold(variant.name), frappe.bold(variant.variant_of) ) ) ``` ### What it specifically checks It exploits the Item doctype's **`variant_of` link field** (each variant item stores its parent template's item code there; a template has it empty). It issues a single self-referential query against `Item` with a **double membership filter**: - `name IN (rule's item codes)` — the row is one of the items added to the rule, **AND** - `variant_of IN (rule's item codes)` — that item's *template* is also among the items added to the rule. Any row matching both conditions means the rule's item list contains a variant and its own template simultaneously. If so, `frappe.throw` aborts the save with: > **"Variant `<variant>` and its template `<template>` cannot both be added to the same Pricing Rule"** (only the first offending pair, `variants[0]`, is reported). Adding the template alone, or only some variants, passes fine — the conflict is detected purely via the `variant_of` parent link, not via `has_variants`. ### Notes - This runs inside `validate()`, so it fires on **every server-side save** (insert and update), not just on submit. - The same `PricingRuleItemCode` child table is shared with **Promotional Scheme** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/promotional_scheme/promotional_scheme.py` also imports it); scheme saves propagate through the generated Pricing Rules, which run this same `validate()`. - The analogous conflict is *not* validated for `apply_on` = "Item Group" or "Brand" — `validate_template_with_variant` is gated explicitly on `apply_on == "Item Code"` (line 159).

final answer
## Short answer The tie‑breaker is the **Stock Ledger Entry's own `creation` timestamp** (row insertion time), used as a secondary sort key after `posting_datetime` in *every* ledger read used by reposting; and on cancellation the whole same‑timestamp "bucket" is deliberately reprocessed in `creation` order after the cancelled voucher's rows have been flagged `is_cancelled = 1`, so the "previous" balance is never taken from an ambiguous sibling. All of this lives in `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`. ## 1. Canonical ordering: `(posting_datetime, creation)` - `get_stock_ledger_entries()` (`stock_ledger.py:1994`) — the workhorse behind `get_previous_sle()`, `get_sle_before_datetime()`/`get_sle_after_datetime()` and `get_future_entries_to_repost()` — ends with: ```sql where is_cancelled = 0 ... order by posting_datetime {order}, creation {order} -- line 2071 ``` - `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()` (`stock_ledger.py:1929`): `order by posting_datetime desc, creation desc limit 1` (line 1959). - Negative-stock scans: `get_future_sle_with_negative_qty()` (`:2419`) does `.orderby(sle.posting_datetime).orderby(sle.creation)`, and the batch variant `get_future_sle_with_negative_batch_qty()` (`:2444`) computes `sum(actual_qty) over (order by posting_datetime, creation)`. - The background item/warehouse reposting queue is Python-sorted identically by `sort_sles()` (`:803`): `key=(get_datetime(d.posting_datetime), get_datetime(d.creation))`. - The schema itself encodes this: `on_doctype_update()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_ledger_entry/stock_ledger_entry.py:366` adds the index `("item_code", "warehouse", "posting_datetime", "creation")`. So a Purchase Receipt and a Material Transfer posted at the same second are ordered by **which SLE row was inserted first** (submission order), not by voucher type/name. ## 2. Picking "previous" vs "current" for the voucher being processed `make_sl_entries()` → `repost_current_voucher()` (`:104`, `:172`) hands `update_entries_after()` (`:587`) the dict `{..., "sle_id": SLE.name, "creation": SLE.creation, "cancelled": ...}`. - **Submit/normal repost**: `initialize_previous_data()` (`:656`) calls `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()`, which — when `args` has `creation` + `sle_id` and is **not** cancelled (`:1943‑1946`) — switches to: ```sql posting_datetime <= T and creation < <my SLE's creation> order by posting_datetime desc, creation desc limit 1 ``` A same-second sibling counts as "previous" **only if it was created earlier**; a sibling created later is treated as *future* — matching `update_qty_in_future_sle()` (`:2212`), whose future condition is `posting_datetime > T OR (posting_datetime == T AND creation > args.creation)` (added only when `not args.is_cancelled`, `:2226‑2229`). The same `creation` tie-break guards the stock-reco boundary helpers `get_next_reco_datetime_condition()` (`:2298`) and `get_datetime_limit_condition()` (`:2347`). - **Cancellation** (e.g., cancelling the Material Transfer): `make_sl_entries()` first calls `set_as_cancel()` (`:241`), which flips `is_cancelled = 1` on the voucher's original SLEs; the reversal rows generated at docstatus 2 also carry `is_cancelled = 1` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:99`). Every read path filters `is_cancelled = 0`, so the dead voucher drops out of the ordering entirely — it can never be selected as "previous" nor contribute to balances. Then `update_entries_after` runs with `cancelled=True`: - `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()` **skips** the `creation <` filter (`:1943` requires `not args.get("cancelled")`) and uses strict `posting_datetime < T` — the running balance starts from the last entry strictly before the shared second. - `build()` (`:709`) → `process_sle_against_current_timestamp()` (`:938`) → `get_sle_against_current_voucher()` (`:1906`): this selects **all** non-cancelled SLEs at exactly that `posting_datetime` for the item/warehouse, `for update`, ordered by `creation asc` — the narrowing `creation == kwargs.creation` is applied **only when not cancelled** (`:1923‑1924`). Hence the surviving sibling (the PR's SLE) and the reversal row are reprocessed *together, in creation order*, each getting its `qty_after_transaction`/valuation/stock queue recomputed in `process_sle()` (`:993`), which chains `self.prev_sle_dict[key] = sle` (`:1164`). - Finally `update_qty_in_future_sle()` bulk-shifts only entries with `posting_datetime > T` for a cancellation (the same-second `creation >` leg is suppressed because `args.is_cancelled` is set) — the same-second bucket was already rebuilt above. ## 3. Why negative-stock validation isn't fooled - **Synchronous check**: in `process_sle()`, `validate_negative_stock()` (`:1352`) evaluates `qty_after_transaction + actual_qty − reserved_stock` against the running balance seeded from the correctly ordered "previous" SLE and grown in `(posting_datetime, creation)` order; failures raise `NegativeStockError` via `raise_exceptions()` (`:1833`). - **Future-facing check**: after reposting, `validate_negative_qty_in_future_sle()` (`:2355`) → `get_future_sle_with_negative_qty()` looks for negative `qty_after_transaction` in *other* vouchers' rows (`voucher_no != current`, `is_cancelled = 0`) ordered by `(posting_datetime, creation)`. Since same-second siblings' balances were recomputed in creation order (and cancelled rows excluded), a surviving transaction that must now sit *after* the reversed entry is judged on its recomputed balance, not on a stale or arbitrarily-ordered one. - **Consistency under concurrency**: the queries take `FOR UPDATE` locks, `validate_cancellation()` (`:213`) refuses to cancel while a `Repost Item Valuation` is "In Progress", and `sle_processing_gate()`/`repost_gate()` (`:276`, `:292`) serialize per-(item, warehouse) reposts so two same-second vouchers can't be chained in opposite orders by racing workers. **Net effect**: ledger position = `(posting_datetime, SLE.creation)`; cancelled vouchers vanish via `is_cancelled = 0` filters; on cancellation the entire same-timestamp bucket is rebuilt in `creation` order from the last strictly-earlier balance — so "current" vs "previous" at an identical posting second is always decided deterministically by row-creation order, and both the per-entry and future negative-stock validations run over that deterministic chain.

I now have the complete picture. Here's how ERPNext resolves this. ## Short answer The ledger's canonical total order for a given `(item_code, warehouse)` is **`(posting_datetime, creation)`** — not `posting_datetime` alone. `creation` (the SLE row's insert timestamp) is the deterministic tiebreaker applied in every "previous"/"current"/"future" query, and on cancellation the cancelled voucher's rows are flagged `is_cancelled = 1` *before* any reposting happens, so they drop out of all ordering/selection queries entirely. Negative-stock validation then re-checks the surviving same-timestamp entries explicitly. ## The mechanics (all in `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`) **1. Canonical ordering everywhere.** `get_stock_ledger_entries()` (line 2065–2081) always sorts `order by posting_datetime {order}, creation {order}`; `update_entries_after.sort_sles()` (line 803–810) sorts the repost deque by `(posting_datetime, creation)`; `get_future_sle_with_negative_batch_qty()` uses a window function `sum(actual_qty) over (order by posting_datetime, creation)`. The schema backs this with a composite index `(item_code, warehouse, posting_datetime, creation)` (`stock_ledger_entry.py::on_doctype_update`, line 366). Timestamps are built via `erpnext/stock/utils.py::get_combine_datetime` (posting_date + posting_time, including fractional seconds — see `test_backdated_sle_with_same_timestamp`, which shows sub-second `posting_time` differences also resolve order; `creation` only kicks in on exact ties). **2. "Previous" SLE selection — `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()` (line 1929–1970).** It returns `order by posting_datetime desc, creation desc limit 1 for update` with three modes: - **Default (`operator="<"`)**: strictly before the posting_datetime. Used when seeding repost state in `initialize_previous_data()` (line 682) and `repost_stock_ledgers()` (line 788–789). - **Reposting a specific SLE** (`args.creation and args.sle_id and not args.cancelled`): operator flips to `<=` **with `creation < '{creation}'`** (lines 1943–1946). This is the crux: at an identical posting timestamp, only entries created *strictly earlier* count as "previous". So when a Material Transfer (created later) is submitted/reposted, the Purchase Receipt posted at the same second but created earlier *is* its previous balance; but when the PR itself is processed, the MT (created later, same second) is *not*. - **`exclude_current_voucher=True`** (used by `get_stock_reco_qty_shift`, line 2286): excludes the voucher by `voucher_no`, so a sibling at the same timestamp can be previous. **3. "Current" SLE selection — `process_sle_against_current_timestamp()` (line 938–942) + `get_sle_against_current_voucher()` (line 1906–1926).** This selects all non-cancelled SLEs at *exactly* the current `posting_datetime`, `orderby(creation asc) for_update`: - **On submit/repost (not cancelled)**: filtered to `doctype.creation == kwargs.creation` — only the current voucher's own rows are "current"; a sibling voucher sharing the second is never swept into the current batch. - **On cancellation** (`cancelled=True`): the creation filter is *dropped*, so **all surviving same-timestamp entries (the Material Transfer) are reprocessed together in creation order** after the cancelled voucher's rows have already been flipped to `is_cancelled=1` by `set_as_cancel()` (line 241–249, runs before any reposting in `make_sl_entries`, line 122–125). The running balance for this bucket is seeded from the entry strictly *before* the shared timestamp (operator `<`, since the `cancelled` flag suppresses the `creation <=` branch). **4. Why cancellation can't be fooled.** Because `set_as_cancel` runs first, every query that orders or selects entries filters `is_cancelled = 0` (`get_stock_ledger_entries` line 2069, `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher` line 1954, `get_sle_against_current_voucher` line 1916, `get_future_sle_with_negative_qty` line 2435). The cancelled PR therefore cannot be picked as anyone's "previous" SLE, and the surviving MT's chain of balances is rebuilt from the pre-10:00:00 state: each reprocessed entry goes through `process_sle()` (line 993), which threads `prev_sle_dict[key] → wh_data` forward (line 1164 re-assigns the just-processed SLE as the next one's previous), and `validate_negative_stock()` (line 1352–1370) checks `wh_data.qty_after_transaction + actual_qty - reserved_stock` per entry, accumulating exceptions that `build()` turns into `NegativeStockError` via `raise_exceptions()` (line 1833–1877) — naming the voucher, date and time of the first offending entry. **5. The "future" shift respects the same tiebreaker — `update_qty_in_future_sle()` (line 2212–2265).** Future = `posting_datetime > X`, **plus** `(posting_datetime == X and creation > args.creation)` — but only when `not args.get("is_cancelled")` (line 2226–2229). On cancellation the tiebreak clause is omitted because the same-timestamp survivors were already recomputed by step 3; only strictly-later entries get the bulk `qty_after_transaction` shift. This exact behavior is pinned by `test_update_qty_in_future_sle_shifts_same_timestamp_later_entry` (`test_stock_ledger_entry.py:1308`): a +5 shift at receipt1's position shifts the same-timestamp/later-creation receipt2 (10 → 35) but not receipt1 itself. Similarly `get_next_stock_reco`/`get_next_reco_datetime_condition` (line 2298–2306) and `get_datetime_limit_condition` (line 2347–2352) treat a same-timestamp Stock Reconciliation as "next"/bounding only if its `creation` is later (test at line 1367). **6. Negative-stock validation after the shift is deliberately *inclusive* of the shared timestamp.** `validate_negative_qty_in_future_sle()` (line 2355) → `get_future_sle_with_negative_qty()` (line 2419–2441) scans `posting_datetime >= args.posting_datetime` (inclusive), `voucher_no != args.voucher_no`, `is_cancelled = 0`, `qty_after_transaction < 0`, ordered by `(posting_datetime, creation)`. Exclusion is by **voucher_no, not timestamp/creation** — so the cancelled voucher can neither hide nor falsely flag, and the same-second MT *is* validated with its recomputed balance. The batched variant does the same with a `(posting_datetime, creation)`-ordered cumulative sum. `validate_previous_sle_qty()` (line 952–968) additionally warns when the *previous* SLE itself already carried a negative balance while the current entry is incoming. **7. Concurrency.** `sle_processing_gate()`/`repost_gate()` (line 269–301, advisory locks per `(item, warehouse)` on Postgres) plus `for update` row locks serialize same-second writers, so `creation` order is well-defined and two vouchers can't both compute from the same stale previous-SLE. **Scenario walk-through** (PR +10 and MT −3, both posted 10:00:00, PR created first; PR cancelled): `set_as_cancel` flags PR's rows → the cancel repost's `get_sle_against_current_voucher` (no creation filter) finds only the MT's rows at 10:00:00, processes them creation-asc from the balance strictly before 10:00:00 (0) → MT recomputes to −3 → `validate_negative_stock` fires → `raise_exceptions` throws `NegativeStockError: "3 units of <Item> needed in <Warehouse> on <date> 10:00:00 for <MT>"`. At no point can the dead PR row be chosen as "previous" or the MT be skipped due to timestamp ambiguity — `creation` pins the order and `is_cancelled=0` removes the dead rows from contention.

I now have the complete picture, confirmed by the dedicated tests. Here's how ERPNext solves the same-timestamp ambiguity: ## The canonical ordering key: `(posting_datetime, creation)` A "second" is not fine-grained enough to order SLEs, so every read of the stock ledger stream uses a two-part sort key. `posting_datetime` is built by `get_combine_datetime()` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py:665`), and note the `test_timestamp_clash` insight: the DB column strips milliseconds, so `02:00:00.1234` and `02:00:00` collide into the *same* bucket. The tie-breaker is the SLE row's `creation` (wall-clock insert time). This ordering is enforced consistently in: - `get_stock_ledger_entries()` — `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:1994` — `order by posting_datetime {order}, creation {order}`, always with `is_cancelled = 0` - `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()` — `stock_ledger.py:1929` — `order by posting_datetime desc, creation desc limit 1 for update` - `update_entries_after.sort_sles()` — `stock_ledger.py:803` — sorts the background repost worklist by `(posting_datetime, creation)` - `get_future_sle_with_negative_qty()` (`stock_ledger.py:2419`) and the batch-window SQL `get_future_sle_with_negative_batch_qty()` (`stock_ledger.py:2444`, `sum(actual_qty) over (order by posting_datetime, creation)`) ## On cancel: the voucher leaves the stream entirely When a voucher is cancelled, `StockLedgerService.get_sl_entries()` (`erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py:99`) sets `is_cancelled: 1` for `docstatus == 2`; `make_sl_entries()` (`stock_ledger.py:104`) then calls `set_as_cancel()` (`stock_ledger.py:241`), flagging **all original SLE rows** of that voucher `is_cancelled = 1`. The negated reversal rows created at cancel time are also born `is_cancelled = 1` (with a fresh, *later* `creation`). Since every previous/current/future query filters `is_cancelled = 0`, both the original and reversal rows drop out of the stream — the surviving sibling at the same second must be recomputed, not trusted. ## How "previous" vs "current" is selected at the same second `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher(args, operator="<")` branches on the cancel state: - **Submitting/validating (not cancelled)** — when the caller has `sle_id` + `creation` and `not args.get("cancelled")`, the operator is forced to `<=` and it adds `and creation < '{args.creation}'` (`stock_ledger.py:1943-1946`). So among same-second SLEs, only rows created **earlier in wall-clock** are "previous". This is what keeps the negative-stock check honest: the Purchase Receipt (created first) is the previous SLE for the Material Transfer created seconds later at the identical posting time, so the transfer validates against the receipt's balance — not against an arbitrarily-picked sibling. - **Cancelling** (`cancelled=True`, threaded from `repost_current_voucher()` at `stock_ledger.py:172`): the creation filter is skipped and the operator stays `<` — "previous" is the last live SLE **strictly before the whole second**. The surviving sibling at that second is deliberately *not* treated as previous; it's reprocessed explicitly: `update_entries_after.build()` (`stock_ledger.py:709`) → `process_sle_against_current_timestamp()` (`stock_ledger.py:938`) → `get_sle_against_current_voucher()` (`stock_ledger.py:1906`) fetches all live SLEs with the identical `(item_code, warehouse, posting_datetime)`, ordered `creation asc`. For a normal submit it restricts to `creation == args.creation` (the voucher's own rows written in one batch); **for a cancel it drops the creation filter**, so the Material Transfer's live SLEs are pulled in and re-run through `process_sle()` on top of the corrected base state, with `frappe.get_doc(sle).db_update()` writing the recomputed `qty_after_transaction` back (`stock_ledger.py:1160-1164`). ## Future-shift and repost boundaries respect the same tie-break - `update_qty_in_future_sle()` (`stock_ledger.py:2212`): "future" = `posting_datetime > T` **or** (`== T` and `creation > args.creation`) — but only when not cancelled. On cancel (`is_cancelled`), it shifts only strictly `posting_datetime > T`, because the reversal row's creation is "now" (later than everything in the bucket), so a creation tie-break would be meaningless there; same-second siblings are handled by the synchronous reprocess above. - `future_sle_exists()` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:705`) detects affected future vouchers with `posting_datetime >= args.posting_datetime` (`>=`, not `>`) — a same-second sibling triggers a `Repost Item Valuation` whose background run (`repost_future_sle` → `get_future_entries_to_repost()` = `get_stock_ledger_entries(kwargs, ">=", "asc", for_update=True)`) reprocesses everything from that second onward in `(posting_datetime, creation)` order. - Stock-reconciliation range bounds use the same logic: `get_next_reco_datetime_condition()` (`stock_ledger.py:2298`) and `get_datetime_limit_condition()` (`stock_ledger.py:2347`). ## Why negative-stock validation isn't fooled `update_entries_after.validate_negative_stock()` (`stock_ledger.py:1352`) and `validate_negative_qty_in_future_sle()` (`stock_ledger.py:2355`) only see the **live** stream (`is_cancelled = 0`) in **creation-tie-broken order**. After the PR is cancelled: (1) its rows are filtered out, (2) the sibling's balances are rebuilt from the last live SLE *before* the second, and (3) any deficit is reported from the first genuinely negative row in that order — so a stale `qty_after_transaction` that still included the cancelled receipt can never masquerade as available (or falsely negative) stock. `sle_processing_gate()`/`repost_gate()` (`stock_ledger.py:276-301`) additionally serialize concurrent writers per `(item, warehouse)` so two same-second vouchers can't race into inconsistent previous-SLE reads. **Proof in tests** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_ledger_entry/test_stock_ledger_entry.py`): `test_tie_breaking` (line 1132 — two Stock Entries at identical `2022-01-01 00:00:01`; cancel the first, repost, and the survivor's `qty_after_transaction` becomes `[1]`), `test_timestamp_clash` (1192), `test_previous_sle_with_clashed_timestamp` (1227), `test_backdated_sle_with_same_timestamp` (1267), `test_update_qty_in_future_sle_shifts_same_timestamp_later_entry` (1308), and `test_get_next_stock_reco_respects_creation_order` (1367).

final answer
I've traced the full mechanism through `erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py` and `erpnext/stock/services/stock_ledger_service.py`. Here's the complete answer. ## The core rule: `creation` is the deterministic tiebreaker inside a posting second Every ledger read/write in the reposting engine orders rows by the composite key **`(posting_datetime, creation)`**, where `creation` is the timestamp at which the SLE *row itself* was inserted — not the voucher's business time. You can see this one rule enforced consistently in every query that decides "current vs previous": | Function | File:line | Ordering | |---|---|---| | `get_stock_ledger_entries()` | `stock_ledger.py:2065-2081` | `where is_cancelled = 0 … order by posting_datetime {order}, creation {order}` | | `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()` | `stock_ledger.py:1948-1961` | `order by posting_datetime desc, creation desc limit 1 for update` | | `get_sle_against_current_voucher()` | `stock_ledger.py:1906-1926` | `orderby(creation, asc)` at an exact `posting_datetime` | | `update_entries_after.sort_sles()` | `stock_ledger.py:803-810` | repost queue sorted by `(get_datetime(posting_datetime), get_datetime(creation))` | | `get_future_sle_with_negative_qty()` | `stock_ledger.py:2438-2439` | `orderby(posting_datetime).orderby(creation)` | | `get_future_sle_with_negative_batch_qty()` | `stock_ledger.py:2450, 2457` | window: `sum(actual_qty) over (order by posting_datetime, creation)` | | `get_next_stock_reco()` / `get_next_reco_datetime_condition()` / `get_datetime_limit_condition()` | `stock_ledger.py:2309, 2298, 2347` | boundary conditions split the `==` case on `creation` | So a Purchase Receipt and a Material Transfer posted at the *same second* are never ambiguous: whichever voucher's SLE rows were **inserted first** (lower `creation`) is ordered first within that timestamp bucket. ## How "previous" is selected — and how cancellation flips the mode `make_sl_entries()` (`stock_ledger.py:104`) detects cancellation via `cancelled = sl_entries[0].get("is_cancelled")` (line 122 — the dicts carry `is_cancelled=1` because `StockLedgerService.get_sl_entries()` sets `is_cancelled: 1 if self.doc.docstatus == 2`, `stock_ledger_service.py:99`). That flag flows through `repost_current_voucher()` (`stock_ledger.py:172-195`), which passes `sle_id`, `creation`, and `cancelled` into `update_entries_after()` (`stock_ledger.py:572`). Then `get_previous_sle_of_current_voucher()` (`stock_ledger.py:1929-1970`) behaves in **two deliberately different modes**: **1. Live submit / non-cancelled repost** — the branch at lines 1943-1946 fires (`args.get("creation") and args.get("sle_id") and not args.get("cancelled")`): - the operator is upgraded from `<` to `<=`, **plus** the extra condition `and creation < '<current SLE creation>'`. - Result: the "previous" balance for the Material Transfer's SLE *includes* the Purchase Receipt's same-second SLE (created earlier → lower `creation`), while anything created at-or-after the current SLE is excluded. The MT correctly sees the PR's stock even though both share the second, and negative-stock validation isn't fooled by ordering. **2. Cancellation** — the branch is deliberately skipped, so the operator stays `<` (strictly before the posting second), and the seed is the last **active** SLE before that instant. Two things make this safe: - Every lookup hard-filters `is_cancelled = 0` (lines 1954, 2069, 1916, 2234, 2435). `set_as_cancel()` (`stock_ledger.py:241-249`) flags the original rows, and the mirrored reversal rows are *also* inserted with `is_cancelled=1` (`stock_ledger_service.py:99`) — so the cancelled voucher contributes nothing to any "previous" baseline; the ledger behaves as if the voucher never existed. - `process_sle_against_current_timestamp()` → `get_sle_against_current_voucher()` then **drops** the `creation == kwargs.creation` filter when cancelled (lines 1923-1924: `if not kwargs.get("cancelled")`), so *all* active SLEs sitting exactly on that posting_datetime — including the surviving neighbour transaction's rows — are re-processed in `creation asc` order via `process_sle()` (`stock_ledger.py:993`), each seeded from `prev_sle_dict` and chained row-to-row (`prev_sle_dict[key] = sle`, line 1164). ## Worked example (PR +10 and MT −10 both at time T, same item/warehouse) - **At MT submit:** seed for the MT's SLE = `posting_datetime <= T AND creation < C_mt` → includes the PR's SLE (C_pr < C_mt) → running balance 10 − 10 = 0 → `validate_negative_stock()` (line 1352, computing `qty_after_transaction + actual_qty − reserved_stock`) passes. - **Cancelling the PR:** its rows (and the reversal rows) vanish behind `is_cancelled = 0`. The seed for the same-second reprocessing is the balance *strictly before* T; the surviving MT SLE recomputes to −10 → `NegativeStockError` raised via `raise_exceptions()` (1833-1877) or `validate_negative_qty_in_future_sle()` (2355) → the cancellation is correctly blocked, instead of being waved through by the PR's ghost +10. - **Cancelling the MT instead:** the reversal rows are inert; the PR's SLE at T is reprocessed alone with the strict-before seed, and its `qty_after_transaction` is rewritten consistently. The future-repost boundary respects the same logic: `update_qty_in_future_sle()` (2212-2263) extends the qty shift into the same second only via `(posting_datetime == T) & (creation > args.creation)` **and only when not cancelled** (line 2226); for cancellations, `get_next_reco_datetime_condition()` switches to a plain `>=` (2298-2306) and same-second survivors are recomputed exactly rather than blindly shifted — with the next Stock Reconciliation capping the range via `get_datetime_limit_condition()` (`posting_datetime < X or (== X and creation < detail.creation)`, 2347-2352). ## Concurrency backstop Because `creation` ties are still possible for truly concurrent writers, `sle_processing_gate(item_code, warehouse)` (`stock_ledger.py:292`) serializes all stock writes per (item, warehouse) — invoked in `make_sl_entries` (lines 118-120, with the item/warehouse pairs **sorted** so two vouchers can't take the gates in opposite order) and in `update_entries_after.__init__` (line 613) — combined with `for update` row locks on every previous-SLE read and `repost_gate()` (276) for background reposts. One telling detail: `make_entry()` (`stock_ledger.py:252-266`) explicitly re-pins `creation` for reposted Stock Reconciliation rows (`sle.db_set("creation", args.get("creation_time"))`, lines 263-264) — confirming that `creation` is the ledger's deliberate ordering anchor, not an incidental column.

I have the complete picture now. Here's the full answer. ## Answer For an intra-company stock transfer, the Purchase Receipt's incoming rate is **taken from the value fixed on the source Delivery Note** — not recomputed fresh at receipt time. The fresh computation only exists as a fallback path for rows without a Delivery Note link. ### Detection of an internal transfer - `InternalTransferService.is_internal_transfer()` — `erpnext/accounts/services/internal_transfer.py:17` — returns True when `is_internal_supplier` is set and `represents_company == company`. - `InternalTransferService.validate_reference()` (same file, line 75) **makes the per-row `delivery_note_item` link mandatory** for internal-transfer Purchase Receipts, and disables pricing rules / tax-included prices. ### Step 1 — The value is fixed at Delivery Note time `SellingController.set_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:515`) computes each `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` from the **source warehouse's stock valuation** via `get_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py:244` — FIFO/LIFO stock queue, Moving Average, or serial/batch valuation). For internal transfers it then forcibly sets `d.rate = d.incoming_rate` (lines 649–667) and zeroes discounts/margin, unless Stock Settings → `allow_internal_transfer_at_arms_length_price` is enabled. This `incoming_rate` is **persisted on the Delivery Note Item row** — that is the value "fixed at DN time". ### Step 2 — PR creation links back to the DN row `make_inter_company_purchase_receipt()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py:409`, via `make_inter_company_transaction`) maps each DN item so `Delivery Note Item.name → Purchase Receipt Item.delivery_note_item` and `target_warehouse → from_warehouse`, and sets `is_internal_supplier = 1` + `inter_company_reference`. Rates are deliberately not copied; they're re-derived on validate. ### Step 3 — PR validation pulls the DN-time rate In `AccountsController.validate()` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:243-244`), after `InternalTransferService.validate()`, `self.set_incoming_rate()` → `BuyingController.set_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:606`) calls `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer()` (line 647): - **Linked case (the normal, mandatory case):** `d.sales_incoming_rate = flt(DN Item.incoming_rate × conversion_factor)` — because `is_internal_supplier` is set, the field fetched is `"incoming_rate"` from the stored Delivery Note Item (lines 683–687). **This is the DN-time value.** - **Fallback only:** if the row has no `delivery_note_item` link, it recomputes fresh via `get_incoming_rate()` against `from_warehouse` at the PR's own posting date/time (lines 660–681). - Then, unless `allow_internal_transfer_at_arms_length_price`, the PR row's `rate` is **overwritten** with `sales_incoming_rate` and discounts/margins zeroed, with an alert "Item rate has been updated as per valuation rate since its an internal stock transfer" (lines 628–645). ### Step 4 — Valuation and stock ledger stay anchored to the DN rate - `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate()` (line 414) uses `item.qty × item.sales_incoming_rate` as the net-rate basis (lines 465–466, 528–530) when computing `valuation_rate` (net rate + valuation taxes + landed-cost amounts, ÷ stock qty). - `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger()` (line 754) posts both legs: outgoing from `from_warehouse` with `outgoing_rate = d.rate`, inward with `incoming_rate = d.valuation_rate` (line 833). - During SLE valuation, `update_entries_after.process_sle` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:1032-1044`) and `get_incoming_outgoing_rate_from_transaction` (line 1467–1472) detect an internal-transfer PR/PI via `is_internal_transfer(sle)` (line 2571) and call `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer()` (line 2540), which **re-anchors both legs to the linked `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate`** (plus per-unit `landed_cost_voucher_amount`) — explicitly to stop a stale `PR.valuation_rate` from leaking valuation gaps into COGS. ### Bottom line The system uses the **Delivery Note-time value**: the stored `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` (the source warehouse's valuation rate at shipment), which is (a) forced into the PR row's `rate`, (b) used as the basis for the PR's `valuation_rate`, and (c) re-asserted at the stock-ledger-entry level. A fresh computation at receipt time via `get_incoming_rate()` occurs only in the fallback branch when no DN item link exists — effectively an edge case, since `validate_reference()` throws if the link is missing on an internal transfer.

final answer
## Answer For an internal transfer, the Purchase Receipt deliberately uses the rate **fixed at the time the source Delivery Note was posted** — not a value recomputed at receipt time. The recomputation path only exists as a fallback for receipt rows that aren't linked to the Delivery Note. ### The flow, end to end **1. Document creation (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py`)** `make_inter_company_purchase_receipt` (line 409) → `make_inter_company_transaction` (line 413) maps Delivery Note → Purchase Receipt, setting `is_internal_supplier = 1` and `inter_company_reference` on the header (lines 470–471). Critically, the item map stores the source row's name in `delivery_note_item` (line 572: `"name": "delivery_note_item"`) — this link is what drives rate resolution later. **2. Rate resolution at PR validate time (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py`)** `AccountsController.validate` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:244`) calls `self.set_incoming_rate()`. The `BuyingController` override (line 606) only kicks in for `Purchase Receipt` (or PI with `update_stock`) when `is_internal_transfer()` is true (internal party + `represents_company == company`, checked in `InternalTransferService.is_internal_transfer`, `erpnext/accounts/services/internal_transfer.py:17`). It then calls `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer` (line 647), which branches per item row: - **Linked row (the normal mapped case):** it reads the value **from the database off the source Delivery Note Item row** (lines 682–687): ```python field = "incoming_rate" if self.get("is_internal_supplier") else "rate" d.sales_incoming_rate = flt(frappe.db.get_value(ref_doctype, d.get(frappe.scrub(ref_doctype)), field) * (d.conversion_factor or 1)) ``` The `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` field is the valuation-based outgoing rate frozen when the DN was validated/submitted — set by `SellingController.set_incoming_rate` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:515`, lines 599–617), which computed it via `get_incoming_rate()` against the from-warehouse stock ledger **at the DN's own posting date/time**. So the PR inherits the DN-time valuation, even if the PR is backdated differently or stock has since changed. - **Unlinked row (manually added):** only here does it compute **fresh** at receipt time — `get_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py`) is called with the PR's own `posting_date`/`posting_time` and the item's `from_warehouse` (lines 659–681). **3. Override and valuation** Unless Stock Settings' `allow_internal_transfer_at_arms_length_price` is enabled (lines 625–629 — in which case the user's entered rate is kept), the item's `rate` is overwritten with `sales_incoming_rate` and discounts/margins are zeroed (lines 631–645). That rate then feeds valuation: in `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` and `get_item_tax_amount` (lines 465–466, 528–532), `net_rate = item.qty * item.sales_incoming_rate` replaces the item's net amount when computing `valuation_rate` (+ item tax + landed-cost amounts), and that becomes the inward SLE's `incoming_rate`. **4. Reinforced at repost time (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py`)** If valuation is ever reposted (`update_entries_after`), both legs of an internal-transfer PR/PI SLE are re-anchored to the same DN-time value: `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer` (line 2540) reads the linked `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` plus any per-unit `landed_cost_voucher_amount` (lines 2547–2568). The comment at lines 1037–1039 explains why: otherwise a stale PR valuation rate "leaks the gap to COGS via divisional_loss." ### Bottom line When the PR comes from the Delivery Note via the mapper, the incoming rate is **the `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` stored at DN time** (a snapshot of the source warehouse's valuation rate then) — fetched directly from the DB, not recomputed at receipt. Fresh computation at the PR's posting moment happens only for rows without a `delivery_note_item` link, and the entire fixed-rate mechanism is bypassed if "Allow internal transfer at arm's length price" is set in Stock Settings. This behavior is pinned by tests like `test_internal_transfer_pr_incoming_sle_anchored_to_dn_rate` and `test_internal_purchase_receipt_incoming_rate_with_lcv` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/test_purchase_receipt.py`.

I now have the complete picture, verified across the controller, mapper, SLE/valuation code and tests. Here's the full answer. ## Summary For an intra-company transfer (Purchase Receipt created against an internal-supplier Delivery Note), the PR's incoming rate is **taken from the value fixed on the source Delivery Note** — specifically `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` (the source warehouse's valuation-based cost captured when the DN was submitted) — **not** recomputed from the stock ledger at receipt time. ## The mechanism, step by step **1. Identifying the transfer and forcing the link** - `make_inter_company_purchase_receipt()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/mapper.py:~470`) sets `target_doc.is_internal_supplier = 1`, `inter_company_reference = DN.name`, and maps each item row with a `delivery_note_item` link. - `InternalTransferService.is_internal_transfer()` (`erpnext/accounts/services/internal_transfer.py:17`) treats it as an internal transfer when `is_internal_supplier` is set and `represents_company == company`. Its `validate_reference()` (L75) **makes the `delivery_note_item` row link mandatory** for internal-transfer PRs ("Please create purchase from internal sale or delivery document itself"). **2. Rate capture during PR validation** - `AccountsController.validate()` calls `self.set_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:244`) → `BuyingController.set_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:606`). - It calls `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer()` (L647). Because the row carries the `delivery_note_item` link, it goes to the **reference branch** (L682–687): ```python field = "incoming_rate" if self.get("is_internal_supplier") else "rate" d.sales_incoming_rate = flt(frappe.db.get_value(ref_doctype, d.delivery_note_item, field) * (d.conversion_factor or 1)) ``` i.e. it reads the **stored** `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` — the cost fixed when the DN was made/submitted. - The fresh-computation branch (L659–681, `get_incoming_rate()` against `from_warehouse` at the **PR's** posting date/time) only runs when a row has *no* DN reference — effectively unreachable for a valid internal-transfer PR due to step 1. - Unless Stock Settings `allow_internal_transfer_at_arms_length_price` is on, `set_incoming_rate()` also zeroes discounts/margins and forces `d.rate = d.sales_incoming_rate` (L631–645). **3. Valuation and SLE** - `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate()` (L414) uses this anchored value: when `item.sales_incoming_rate` is set, `net_rate = item.qty * item.sales_incoming_rate` (L465–466) instead of the billed net amount, so `valuation_rate = (net_rate + item_tax_amount + LCV amount) / stock_qty`. - On submit, `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger()` (L754) creates the inward SLE at the receiving warehouse with `incoming_rate: d.valuation_rate` (L833), paired with the outward SLE at `from_warehouse` (`outgoing_rate: d.rate`, L785, linked via `dependant_sle_voucher_detail_no`). **4. Where the DN's fixed value comes from, and drift protection** - On the DN side, `SellingController` recomputes `d.incoming_rate = get_incoming_rate(...)` from the source warehouse at DN posting time (selling_controller.py ~L599), and on any later backdated repost `update_rate_on_delivery_and_sales_return()` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:1558`) writes the recomputed outgoing rate back into the DN row — so the stored DN rate stays the single source of truth. - On repost, `RepostItemValuation._recalculate_valuation_rate()` (`repost_item_valuation.py:369–376`) explicitly re-runs `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer()` for `is_internal_supplier` docs, and `update_rate_on_purchase_receipt()` (`stock_ledger.py:1574–1588`) resets `PR Item.valuation_rate` to the SLE's `outgoing_rate`. **Proof in tests:** `test_internal_transfer_pr_incoming_sle_anchored_to_dn_rate` (`test_purchase_receipt.py:1912`) states it verbatim: *"Internal-transfer PR's inward SLE must use DN.incoming_rate even when PR.item.valuation_rate was wrong at submit, so divisional_loss does not leak to COGS."* Even when the DB is artificially corrupted (`sales_incoming_rate=0`, `valuation_rate=80`), `update_entries_after` restores the SLE to the DN's rate (100). The backdated-transfer test (L1764–1791) similarly shows `valuation_rate` following the DN's reposted cost (200) while `rate` stays at the originally fixed 100. The GL counterpart is `make_divisional_loss_gl_entry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/gl_composer.py:233`), which books any billing-vs-stock-value gap to the divisional-loss account — the reason the anchor exists. **Bottom line:** the PR does *not* compute a fresh rate from the ledger at receipt time; it inherits `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` (fixed at DN time, kept correct across reposts), overriding the item's billed `rate` unless arms-length internal pricing is explicitly allowed.

final answer
## Answer For an intra-company internal‑transfer Purchase Receipt, the incoming rate is **not recomputed from the source warehouse at receipt time** — it is **anchored to the `incoming_rate` that was computed and stored on the source Delivery Note Item when the DN was made**. A "fresh at receipt time" calculation exists only as an unlinked fallback that validation effectively rules out. Here is the full chain: ### 1. What qualifies as an intra-company internal transfer `InternalTransferService.is_internal_transfer()` (`erpnext/accounts/services/internal_transfer.py:17-27`): a Purchase Receipt qualifies when `is_internal_supplier` is set **and** `represents_company == company`. The stock-ledger mirror `is_internal_transfer(sle)` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:2571-2580`) checks the same flags on the voucher. ### 2. Validation forces the DN linkage In `AccountsController.validate` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:213`), line 243 runs `InternalTransferService(self).validate()`, whose `validate_reference()` (`internal_transfer.py:75-102`) demands that the PR carry `inter_company_reference` **and** a `delivery_note_item` link on every item row — otherwise it throws *"Internal Sale or Delivery Reference missing. Please create purchase from internal sale or delivery document itself."* Separately, `StockInternalTransferService.validate_internal_transfer` (`erpnext/stock/services/internal_transfer.py:24-61`, called from `StockController.validate`, `stock_controller.py:61`) makes `from_warehouse` mandatory on every row. ### 3. Rate override on the PR — `BuyingController.set_incoming_rate` `erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:606-645` (invoked from `AccountsController.validate` line 244). After early-exits (non-PR/PI, no `update_stock`, returns, non-internal transfers), it calls `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer` (`buying_controller.py:647-687`), which sets `d.sales_incoming_rate` in one of two ways: - **Linked case (the enforced, normal case):** `field = "incoming_rate" if self.get("is_internal_supplier") else "rate"`, then `d.sales_incoming_rate = flt(frappe.db.get_value("Delivery Note Item", d.delivery_note_item, field) * (d.conversion_factor or 1))` — a **stored value read off the source Delivery Note Item row**, fixed at DN time. - **Unlinked fallback:** if the row has no `delivery_note_item` reference, it computes the outgoing rate **fresh** via `get_incoming_rate()` (`erpnext/stock/utils.py:244`) against `warehouse: d.from_warehouse` with the **PR's** posting date/time and `qty: -1 * stock_qty` — i.e., a live valuation of the source warehouse at receipt time. Because `validate_reference` (step 2) requires DN-item links on non-return internal-transfer PRs, this branch is effectively unreachable for submitted internal transfers. Then, unless **Stock Settings → `allow_internal_transfer_at_arms_length_price`** is enabled, it zeroes `discount_percentage`, `discount_amount`, `margin_rate_or_amount` and forces `d.rate = d.sales_incoming_rate` (*"Row #x: Item rate has been updated as per valuation rate since its an internal stock transfer"*). ### 4. Where that DN value came from `SellingController.set_incoming_rate` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:515-667`): when the Delivery Note itself is an internal transfer, the condition at line 590-598 (`... or self.is_internal_transfer() ...`) forces `d.incoming_rate = get_incoming_rate({warehouse: d.warehouse, qty: -1*qty, posting_date/time of the DN, ...})` — the source warehouse's valuation captured **once at DN validation** and persisted on the DN Item row — and then (lines 638-667) forces `d.rate = d.incoming_rate * conversion_factor`, zeroing discounts/margins. ### 5. PR valuation and the stock ledger - `BuyingController.update_valuation_rate` (`buying_controller.py:414-490`): for internal transfers `net_rate = item.qty * item.sales_incoming_rate` (lines 465-466), so `valuation_rate = (net_rate + item_tax_amount + landed_cost_voucher_amount) / qty_in_stock_uom` — DN-derived value plus valuation taxes/landed cost. - `BuyingController.update_stock_ledger` (`buying_controller.py:754-893`) posts **two SLEs** per row: an outgoing leg at `from_warehouse` (`outgoing_rate: d.rate`, `recalculate_rate: 1`, lines 780-792) and the incoming leg (`incoming_rate: d.valuation_rate` with `recalculate_rate: 1` because `from_warehouse` is set, lines 831-838). For serial/batch items the inbound bundle is cloned from the DN side via `get_package_for_target_warehouse` → `make_bundle_for_material_transfer` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:860-911`) → `SerialandBatchBundle.set_incoming_rate` (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:393` → `set_incoming_rate_for_inward_transaction:781`). - Crucially, `process_sle` (`erpnext/stock/stock_ledger.py:993`, anchor at **1032-1044**) then **overrides both legs** with the DN value: for PR/PI SLEs where `is_internal_transfer(sle)`, `rate = get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer(sle)`, assigned to `sle.outgoing_rate` (negative-qty leg) or `sle.incoming_rate` (inward leg). The code comment states the intent verbatim: *"Anchor both legs of an internal-transfer PR/PI to the DN/SI incoming_rate; otherwise an inward SLE that inherits a stale PR.valuation_rate leaks the gap to COGS via divisional_loss."* - `get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer` (`stock_ledger.py:2540-2568`) reads the linked `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate` plus `landed_cost_voucher_amount / abs(actual_qty)`. The same function is reused during reposting by `get_incoming_outgoing_rate_from_transaction` (`stock_ledger.py:1467-1472`), so even future reposts re-read the stored DN value instead of revaluing the source warehouse. ### Bottom line The system uses the **value fixed at source-DN time** (the `Delivery Note Item.incoming_rate`, captured by `SellingController.set_incoming_rate` at DN validation and propagated through `BuyingController.set_incoming_rate` → `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer` → `update_valuation_rate` → `process_sle`/`get_incoming_rate_for_inter_company_transfer`). The "computed fresh at receipt time" path (`get_incoming_rate` against `from_warehouse` in `set_sales_incoming_rate_for_internal_transfer`) is only a fallback for rows without a DN-item link, which validation rejects for internal transfers. The `allow_internal_transfer_at_arms_length_price` Stock Setting only frees the **billed** `rate` from the override — the stock valuation and both SLE legs remain anchored to the DN's stored incoming rate. (Contrast: a genuinely *inter-company* transfer, where the supplier represents a different company, skips all of this and prices the PR from its own `valuation_rate`.)
