I now have the complete picture. Here's the answer: ## Short answer **There is a submit-time batch-expiry validation, but it is deliberately bypassed for exactly the two scenarios you asked about** — `Material Issue` and `Material Transfer` Stock Entries. For those purposes ERPNext does **not** throw on an expired batch (by design, so expired stock can be issued/written off); for all other purposes it does throw. ## The validation that exists **`SerialBatchBundleService.validate_serialized_batch()`** — `erpnext/stock/services/serial_batch_bundle_service.py:106-147` It is wired into the validation chain twice: - `StockController.validate()` → `sbb.validate_serialized_batch()` (`erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:57`) — runs on every save *and* submit of any stock voucher - `StockEntry.validate()` → `sbb.validate_serialized_batch()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.py:318`) For each row with `qty > 0`, a `batch_no`, a `posting_date`, and `docstatus < 2`, it fetches `Batch.expiry_date` and: ```python if expiry_date and getdate(expiry_date) < getdate(self.doc.posting_date): frappe.throw( _("Row #{0}: The batch {1} has already expired.")..., BatchExpiredError, ) ``` `BatchExpiredError` is defined in `erpnext/exceptions.py:46` (subclass of `frappe.ValidationError`) and re-exported from `erpnext/controllers/stock_controller.py:27`. The check is posting-date-aware, not just "today"-aware. The test `test_batch_expiry` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/test_stock_entry.py:1958-1982`) proves it fires — but note it uses purpose **"Material Receipt"**, one of the non-skipped purposes. ## Why issue/transfer is exempt The same method opens with: ```python is_material_issue = False if self.doc.doctype == "Stock Entry" and self.doc.purpose in ["Material Issue", "Material Transfer"]: is_material_issue = True ... if is_material_issue: continue # skips the expiry throw for these rows ``` So `Material Issue` and `Material Transfer` rows fall through past the `BatchExpiredError` check entirely. This is clearly intentional, not an oversight: 1. **UI filter override** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/stock_entry.js:129-131` explicitly sets `filters["include_expired_batches"] = 1` for purposes `Material Receipt / Material Transfer / Material Issue`, so the batch link-field query (`erpnext.controllers.queries.get_batch_no`) *includes* expired batches — the `expiry_date >= posting_date` filter at `erpnext/controllers/queries.py:588-589` and `652-654` is skipped when that flag is set. 2. **Helper button** — `stock_entry.js:511-542` adds an **"Expired Batches"** button on Material Issue entries that calls `get_expired_batch_items()` → `get_expired_batches()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry/services/serial_batch.py:339-373`, which queries `Batch` where `expiry_date <= nowdate()`) and auto-fills the items grid with expired batches holding stock — i.e., ERPNext actively helps you issue expired stock out. ## Related but narrower check `StockEntryDetail.validate_batch()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/stock_entry_detail/stock_entry_detail.py:88-99`) throws `"Batch {0} of Item {1} has expired."` when `posting_date > expiry_date` (plus a disabled-batch throw), but `StockEntry.validate_batch()` (`stock_entry.py:1479-1487`) only invokes it for purposes `Material Transfer for Manufacture`, `Manufacture`, `Repack`, and `Send to Subcontractor` — again not for Material Issue/Transfer. ## The Serial-and-Batch-Bundle path If you use the modern bundle flow (`serial_and_batch_bundle` instead of the legacy `batch_no` field), `SerialandBatchBundle.validate()` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/serial_and_batch_bundle/serial_and_batch_bundle.py:109-145`) performs **no expiry throw** on its entries either; expired batches are only *filtered out of auto-selection/query helpers* — `get_non_expired_batches()` (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:2570`) and the FIFO/batch queries with `expiry_date >= today() | isnull()` conditions (`serial_and_batch_bundle.py:3173`, `3518`). **Bottom line:** for *receiving* onto an expired batch (and Manufacture/Repack/Subcontractor flows) ERPNext throws `BatchExpiredError` at save/submit, but for *issuing or transferring* via Stock Entry the validation is explicitly skipped and the UI even assists in selecting expired batches — you can move expired stock between warehouses or issue it out without any server-side block.

final answer
## Short answer **No.** Submitting a Sales Order in ERPNext does **not** automatically email the customer a confirmation. There is no email/notification code anywhere in the Sales Order submit path, and ERPNext ships no default notification that does this. Customer-facing emails on Sales Orders are always either **manually triggered** (the Email button on the form) or **opt-in via a user-configured Frappe "Notification"**. ## What I verified in the code **1. The controller's `on_submit` sends no email** — `SalesOrder.on_submit()` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` (line 450) only does transactional housekeeping: - `super().update_prevdoc_status()`, `check_credit_limit()`, `update_reserved_qty()` - `DeliveryScheduleService(self).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items()` - Authorization Control check, `update_project()`, `update_blanket_order()` - inter-company order linking, coupon-code counting, and `create_stock_reservation_entries()` (if "Reserve Stock" is enabled) There is no `frappe.sendmail`, no email template lookup, nothing customer-facing. Similarly, the parent controllers under `erpnext/controllers/` (`selling_controller.py`, `accounts_controller.py`, etc.) contain no `frappe.sendmail` calls, and `sales_order.json` has no `email_template` / auto-email field. **2. Nothing at the hook layer either** — in `erpnext/hooks.py`: - The `doc_events` wildcard `"*"` entry (line 368–373) only registers `validate` hooks (`service_level_agreement.apply`, `transaction_deletion_record.check_for_running_deletion_job`). - There is **no `"Sales Order"` entry with `on_submit`** in `doc_events` (the only `on_submit` hook is for Stock Entry). - The `Sales Order` reference at line 270 is just the customer-portal website route (`/orders`), not an email trigger. **3. No pre-packaged Notification fixtures** — a search across the repo found no `Notification` records, fixtures, or setup-wizard code that auto-creates a "Sales Order submitted → email customer" notification. ## Where emails *can* be triggered instead - **Manually from the UI:** the standard **Email** toolbar button on the Sales Order form (provided by Frappe Desk's form toolbar, not ERPNext-specific code) opens the compose dialog and sends the chosen Print Format (e.g., "Sales Order") as a PDF to the customer's contact email. This is user-initiated, not part of submission. - **Configurable automation (opt-in):** Frappe's **Notification doctype** (`frappe/email/doctype/notification`, in the Frappe framework repo, not ERPNext) can send emails on document events — you'd create a Notification with Document Type = "Sales Order", Event = "Submit", Channel = "Email", and attach an Email Template. Frappe's generic submit flow (`frappe/model/document.py` → `Document.submit()` → `on_submit` → event hooks) invokes these configured notifications, which is the only supported way to get an automatic customer confirmation email. Until a site admin creates such a Notification, nothing is sent. So if you're seeing (or expecting) confirmation emails on Sales Order submission on a given site, it's coming from a locally configured Notification (or a custom app hook), not from ERPNext's out-of-the-box submit flow.

## Answer: No — ERPNext does **not** automatically email the customer when a Sales Order is submitted There is no built-in customer confirmation email in the Sales Order submit flow. Emailing the customer only happens via opt-in mechanisms. ### Evidence from the submit flow **`SalesOrder.on_submit()`** — `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py` (lines 450–471) — contains zero email logic. It only does: - `super().update_prevdoc_status()` (updates the source Quotation) - `self.check_credit_limit()` - `self.update_reserved_qty()` - `DeliveryScheduleService(self).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items()` - Authorization Control validation (`validate_approving_authority`) - `update_project()`, `update_blanket_order()` - `update_linked_doc(...)` (inter-company order) - coupon code count update, `create_stock_reservation_entries()` A grep of the whole `sales_order.py` for `email`/`sendmail`/`payment_request` finds only the `contact_email` field definition — no `frappe.sendmail` call anywhere. **Hooks don't add one either** — `erpnext/hooks.py`: - The `doc_events` dict (line 367+) has no `"Sales Order"` entry (only `"*"`, period-closing doctypes, `Stock Entry`, `User`, `Communication`, etc.). - "Sales Order" appears at line 364 in `pre_submit_validation_doctypes`, which merely wires `erpnext.accounts.utils.pre_submit_validation` on `validate` — an accounting check, not email. - ERPNext ships only two Notification fixtures repo-wide: `erpnext/setup/.../notification_for_new_fiscal_year` and `erpnext/manufacturing/notification/material_request_receipt_notification` — neither relates to Sales Orders or customers. ### How a customer email *would* be triggered (all opt-in) 1. **Notification / Email Alert (standard way):** an admin creates a **Notification** doc in Frappe core (`frappe/email/doctype/notification`) with event "Submit" for Sales Order, recipients from `contact_email`, and an attached print format. Frappe fires these during `doc.save()/submit()` — but only if someone configured one; nothing ships by default. 2. **Manual "Email" button** on the SO form → `frappe.core.doctype.communication.email.make` (client-side, `erpnext/public/js/controllers/transaction.js`). 3. **Payment Request** — `make_payment_request()` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py` (line 723) → `PaymentRequest.send_email()` (lines 587–611, called from the PR's own `before_submit`) emails the customer a payment link. But this is triggered explicitly from the "Request Payment" action (`make_payment_request()` in `transaction.js`, line 485) or via webshop checkout — never as a side effect of submitting the Sales Order. So if a customer confirmation email arrives after SO submission, it's coming from a manually configured Notification/Email Alert or a Payment Request — not from anything ERPNext does automatically on submit.

## Answer: No — submitting a Sales Order does **not** automatically email the customer. There is no built-in confirmation email on submit. ### Evidence from the submit flow **1. `SalesOrder.on_submit()` — `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450-471`** This is the entire doctype-level submit hook, and it contains no email/notification logic at all: - `update_prevdoc_status()`, `check_credit_limit()`, `update_reserved_qty()` - `DeliveryScheduleService(self).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items()` - `Authorization Control.validate_approving_authority()` - `update_project()`, `update_blanket_order()` - `update_linked_doc()` for inter-company orders, `update_coupon_code_count()` - `create_stock_reservation_entries()` if `reserve_stock` is set **2. No email in the controller chain.** The parent `AccountsController` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py`) doesn't even define an `on_submit`, and a search of the whole `erpnext/controllers/` directory (`SellingController`, `TransactionBase`, `AccountsController`, etc.) turns up **zero** `frappe.sendmail`/`send_email` calls. There is no `send_email` in `sales_order.js` either. **3. No hook-based email.** In `erpnext/hooks.py`, the `doc_events` map (line 367+) registers `on_submit` handlers for Stock Entry, Sales Invoice (regional tax hooks), etc. — but there is **no `"Sales Order"` entry at all**, so nothing fires on SO submit beyond the class method above. ERPNext also ships no default `Notification` (frappe.automation) fixtures with a "Submit" event for Sales Order. ### Where customer emails *are* sent, for context - **Manual "Email" button** — the standard Frappe document-email dialog on the Sales Order form (`frappe.core.doctype.communication.email.make` in the framework, not ERPNext). User-initiated only. - **Payment Request email** — `PaymentRequest.send_email()` at `erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py:587` ("send email with payment link") is the closest thing to an order email. It's called from `validate` (line 266) when a Payment Request document is *created* with a payment gateway and `mute_email` is unset — but Payment Requests are only created explicitly (button, POS, portal checkout), never automatically as a consequence of Sales Order submit. Note `PaymentRequest.on_submit` (line 269) only updates advance payment status; the email goes out on creation, and nothing auto-creates the Payment Request. ### How to get the behavior To email the customer on SO submit you'd have to configure it yourself: create a **Notification** document (frappe.automation, event = Submit) with an Email channel, or add a custom `on_submit` hook via `doc_events` in `hooks.py` / a custom app. Out of the box, ERPNext leaves Sales Order confirmation emails to the user.

final answer
## Short answer **No.** In stock ERPNext, submitting a Sales Order does **not** automatically email the customer a confirmation. Nothing in the Sales Order submit chain — neither the document class's `on_submit`, nor any `doc_events` hook, nor a shipped fixture — sends email. Emailing the customer is always either **user-initiated** (the form's Email button / print‑and‑email dialog) or **opt-in** via a manually configured Notification record in the Frappe framework. ## What the submit flow actually does The generic submit lives in the Frappe framework (outside this repo: `frappe/model/document.py` → `Document.submit()` → `docstatus = 1` → `run_post_save_methods()` → calls `on_submit`). Inside this repo, `SalesOrder.on_submit` at **`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450–471`** does only: - `super().update_prevdoc_status()` (e.g. closes the linked Quotation) - `self.check_credit_limit()` → `check_credit_limit()` (`erpnext/accounts/Party` credit-limit check) - `self.update_reserved_qty()` - `DeliveryScheduleService(self).delete_removed_delivery_schedule_items()` - `frappe.get_cached_doc("Authorization Control").validate_approving_authority(...)` - `self.update_project()`, `self.update_prevdoc_status("submit")`, `self.update_blanket_order()` - `update_linked_doc(...)` for the inter-company order reference - `update_coupon_code_count(...)` if a coupon was used - `self.create_stock_reservation_entries()` if `reserve_stock` is set There is **zero** email code here — the only "email" token in the whole file is the `contact_email` data field (line 82), and `erpnext/controllers/` (the `SellingController → StockController → AccountsController` chain the class inherits through) contains no `frappe.sendmail`/`send_email` calls either. ## Hook layer — also no email In **`erpnext/hooks.py`**, the `doc_events` map (lines 367–439) has **no `on_submit` entry for Sales Order at all**. Sales Order appears only in: - `pre_submit_validation_doctypes` (lines 359–365) → `"validate": "erpnext.accounts.utils.pre_submit_validation"` (lines 377–379) - the `"*"` wildcard `validate` hooks: SLA application and the transaction-deletion-job check The only `on_submit` doc_events anywhere are `Stock Entry` (material-request qty sync, line 380) and the Italy regional `Sales Invoice` handler (line 405) — neither emails the customer. The `notification_config` hook (line 73, → `erpnext.startup.notifications.get_notification_config`) is **not** an email mechanism: `erpnext/startup/notifications.py:19` merely registers `"Sales Order": {"status": ("not in", ("Completed", "Closed")), "docstatus": ("<", 2)}` as a filter for the **in-app bell-icon notification list** for logged-in users. There are also no shipped `Notification` fixtures (no `fixtures` entry in hooks.py, no fixture JSONs matching notifications). ## How a customer *does* get an SO email (all opt-in, all in the Frappe framework, not this repo) 1. **Notification doctype** (`frappe/email/doctype/notification/notification.py`) — a user must create a Notification with Type = Email and Event = Submit for "Sales Order". Frappe's generic trigger fires it for any doctype's submit, but ERPNext ships none by default. 2. **Document Follow** (`frappe.email.doctype.document_follow`) — daily email digest, only for users who explicitly follow the document. 3. **Manual Email button** on the Sales Order form — creates a Communication via `frappe.core.doctype.communication.email.make` and sends the chosen print format; strictly user-triggered. 4. Related-but-distinct: **Payment Request** (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/payment_request/payment_request.py`) can email the customer a payment link, but it is created on demand (Payment button / POS), never auto-created at SO submit — hooks.py only registers `validate_payment` for "Integration Request" (line 437), with no SO `on_submit` hook for payment requests. Notably, even **Sales Invoice** has no automatic customer email in this codebase — its submit path (controller + `sales_invoice.js`) contains no email trigger either, so email on submit is consistently a configuration/manual concern, never a built-in behavior.

final answer
## Short answer **No.** Purchase Order has no supplier‑side counterpart to the customer credit limit. The `Supplier` doctype has no `credit_limit` field at all (ERPNext never auto‑caps a PO by how much the company already owes a supplier). But PO submission *is* gated — by three mechanisms of a fundamentally different nature: ## 1. Budget validation — a spend cap keyed to accounting dimensions, not the supplier - `PurchaseOrder.on_submit()` → `self.validate_budget()` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:386`) - `BuyingController.validate_budget()` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978`) dispatches to `BudgetValidation` (`erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py`, class at line 13) unless "use_legacy_budget_controller" is set in Accounts Settings, in which case the legacy `validate_expense_against_budget()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py:377`). - It sums the PO's ordered amount **plus** already‑submitted unbilled POs, un‑ordered purchase Material Requests, and actual GL expense (`get_ordered_amount`, `get_requested_amount`, `get_actual_expense`) for the fiscal year, keyed by `(dimension_type, dimension, GL account)` — Cost Center/Project + expense account — against submitted `Budget` records. - If the Budget's `action_if_annual_budget_exceeded` / `action_if_accumulated_monthly_budget_exceeded` is `Stop`, `BudgetValidation.stop()` raises `frappe.throw(msg, BudgetError, title="Budget Exceeded")` (lines 292–293), aborting the submit; `Warn` only msgprints. Users holding the Company's `exception_budget_approver_role` get a warning instead of a block. - Nuance: the code comments that for PO/Material Request this runs *after* docstatus=1 (inside `on_submit`), but since Frappe executes submission in one DB transaction, the throw still rolls the submission back — so it does gate submission. ## 2. Authorization Control — a monetary cap on the *submitting user*, not the supplier - Immediately after, `PurchaseOrder.on_submit()` (`purchase_order.py:388`) calls `frappe.get_cached_doc("Authorization Control").validate_approving_authority(self.doctype, self.company, self.base_grand_total)`. - `AuthorizationControl.validate_approving_authority()` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154`) evaluates `Authorization Rule` records (thresholds on "Grand Total", "Average Discount", etc., per user/role/company). If the PO total exceeds a rule's `value`, the current user must hold the matching `approving_role`/`approving_user`, else it throws "Not authorized since Grand Total exceeds limits". - This is the closest thing to a "spend limit" on the buying side, but it limits **who may commit the money**, never the counterparty. ## 3. Supplier Scorecard — the only supplier‑facing gate, and it's qualitative - `PurchaseOrder.validate()` → `validate_supplier()` (`purchase_order.py:272–292`): reads the `prevent_pos` / `warn_pos` flags on `Supplier` (pushed from `Supplier Scorecard` standings by `supplier_scorecard.py:144–146`). If `prevent_pos` is set, it throws *"Purchase Orders are not allowed for {supplier} due to a scorecard standing of {status}"*; `warn_pos` shows an orange caution. Binary performance‑standing gate with no amount involved. ## How this differs from the Sales Order credit limit The SO check is `SalesOrder.on_submit()` → `SalesOrder.check_credit_limit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:452, 514`) → module‑level `check_credit_limit(customer, company, ...)` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514`), using `get_credit_limit()` (line 802) which reads the customer's company‑wise `Customer Credit Limit` child rows (with `bypass_credit_limit_check`), falling back to the Company default `credit_limit`, and throws *"Credit limit has been crossed for customer…"* unless the user holds the Accounts Settings `credit_controller` role. There's also an optional pre‑submit warning path: `pre_submit_validation` → `_check_credit_limit_warn` (`erpnext/accounts/utils.py:2774, 2805`, hooked via `erpnext/hooks.py:359–379` when Accounts Settings "preview_mode" is on) — Purchase Order is deliberately **not** in `pre_submit_validation_doctypes`. The essential difference is **who is being protected and against what**: | Mechanism | Limit measured against | Nature | |---|---|---| | Customer credit limit (SO) | One customer's outstanding receivables | External **counterparty exposure** cap | | Budget (PO) | Expense account / cost center / project, per fiscal year | Internal **expense** cap, supplier‑agnostic | | Authorization Control (PO) | The submitting user/role's monetary authority | Internal **delegation‑of‑authority** rule | | Supplier Scorecard (PO) | The supplier's performance standing | Qualitative **allow/deny**, not an amount | So the asymmetry is by design: ERPNext guards receivables with a monetary per‑customer limit, while the buying side is controlled by internal budget and approval‑authority mechanisms plus a binary supplier scorecard — there is no automatic "supplier payable limit" check anywhere in the PO lifecycle.

final answer
## Answer **No — Purchase Order has no supplier-side credit-limit equivalent.** ERPNext never checks a supplier's cumulative spend/outstanding exposure against a stored monetary ceiling. There is no `check_credit_limit`-style call anywhere in the buying stack: a search for `credit_limit` / `spend_limit` / `purchase_limit` across `erpnext/buying/` returns zero hits, and the Supplier doctype (`erpnext/buying/doctype/supplier/supplier.json`) has no monetary-limit field at all. ### The reference behavior: Sales Order's credit limit - `SalesOrder.on_submit` → `SalesOrder.check_credit_limit` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:514-524`) → `check_credit_limit(customer, company)` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514-571`. - It compares two things: a **monetary ceiling** from `get_credit_limit` (`Customer Credit Limit` child table per company, falling back to Customer Group, then Accounts Settings `default_credit_limit`), and the customer's **live outstanding balance** from `get_customer_outstanding` (`customer.py:706`), computed from GL Entries (`SUM(debit) − SUM(credit)` where `party_type = Customer`) plus unlinked/unbilled amounts. If outstanding > limit it `frappe.throw`s unless the current user holds the `credit_controller` role (Accounts Settings). This is a **counterparty financial-risk control** — the party's own indebtedness vs. a limit stored on the party. ### What actually gates Purchase Order submission Three mechanisms, none of which is a supplier credit limit: 1. **Supplier Scorecard standing** — `PurchaseOrder.validate_supplier` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:272-294`), called from `PurchaseOrder.validate` (line 200), i.e., a pre-submit validation. It reads `Supplier.prevent_pos` / `warn_pos`, which are pushed by `SupplierScorecard.apply_standing` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/supplier_scorecard/supplier_scorecard.py:137-146`) based on the supplier's weighted performance score (quality/delivery criteria across scoring periods). Block or warn, keyed to the supplier — but **binary and performance-based, no amount involved**. 2. **Budget validation** — `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` (line 386) → `BuyingController.validate_budget` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978-1000`) → `BudgetValidation` (`erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py`). It sums un-billed ordered amounts of submitted POs per (dimension, GL expense account) for the fiscal year (`get_ordered_amount`, lines 209-237) against the **Budget** doctype, and stops or warns per budget action (`handle_purchase_order_overlimit`, line 342). Monetary, but keyed on **internal accounting dimensions** (expense account / cost center / project), completely supplier-agnostic. 3. **Authorization Control** — `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` (lines 388-390) → `AuthorizationControl.validate_approving_authority(self.doctype, self.company, self.base_grand_total)` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154-237`). It matches `Authorization Rule` records whose threshold `value` ≤ the document grand total and requires the *submitting user* to be the rule's `approving_user` or hold its `approving_role`, else throws "Not authorized since Grand Total exceeds limits / Can be approved by …". This is the closest thing to a "spend limit" — amount-based — but it constrains the **user**, not the supplier. (Sales Order calls the same method at `sales_order.py:456`, so this isn't even the SO/PO asymmetry.) ### How they differ in nature | | SO credit limit | PO-side gates | |---|---|---| | What is limited | The **counterparty's** cumulative exposure | Supplier standing (non-monetary), internal budget, or approver authority | | Measured quantity | Live AR balance from GL ledger + unbilled orders | Supplier score → standing band; unbilled ordered amount per expense account/FY; doc grand total vs. rule threshold | | Where the ceiling lives | On the party (`Customer Credit Limit`, per company/group) | On `Supplier Scorecard` standings, `Budget` records, or `Authorization Rule` values | | Amount-based? | Yes, and cumulative against party balance | Scorecard: no; Budget: yes but internal; Authorization: yes but per-user | In short: PO submission *is* gated — by supplier scorecard standing (at validate), budget consumption, and authorization rules (at submit) — but ERPNext models purchase-side control as **internal fiscal/authority discipline plus vendor performance**, not as a credit-exposure limit on the supplier, because a supplier's "outstanding" isn't a risk to you the way a customer's receivable balance is.

## Answer **Short version:** No — Purchase Order has **no supplier-side spend-limit equivalent** of the customer credit limit. The Supplier doctype has no credit/spend-limit field at all. What does gate a PO's financial commitment is a **budget check** (plus a generic **Authorization Control** approval cap) — and both are of a fundamentally different nature than a credit limit. ### One nuance on the premise first In this codebase the SO credit-limit check doesn't live in `validate()` — it fires inside the submit transaction: `SalesOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450–452`) calls `self.check_credit_limit()` → `check_credit_limit(customer, company)` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514`. It's enforced "before submission" only in the sense that a `frappe.throw` inside `on_submit` rolls back the whole submit atomically (a draft can be saved freely; the limit bites when you submit). The limit is resolved by `get_credit_limit()` (`customer.py:802`): per-company `Customer Credit Limit` row on the Customer → Customer Group limit (unless `bypass_credit_limit_check`) → Company default `credit_limit`, then compared against the customer's outstanding exposure. Users holding the `Accounts Settings.credit_controller` role bypass it; others get a blocking exception with a "Send Email to controller" action. ### What gates Purchase Order submission 1. **Budget check (the real PO-side control)** — `PurchaseOrder.on_submit()` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:386`) → `BuyingController.validate_budget()` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978–1000`). If `Accounts Settings.use_legacy_budget_controller` is off, it instantiates the new **`BudgetValidation`** controller (`erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py:13`); otherwise it calls the legacy `validate_expense_against_budget()` from `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py` per item row (only at `docstatus == 1`, i.e., at submit). `BudgetValidation` matches submitted `Budget` docs by company + expense account + accounting dimensions (cost center, project, plus any custom "Accounting Dimension") for the fiscal year of the PO's `transaction_date`, then aggregates three spend streams for that key: - **ordered amount** — unbilled amounts on other submitted, non-closed Purchase Orders (`get_ordered_amount`, L209), - **requested amount** — pending Material Requests against that account (`get_requested_amount`, L239), - **actual expense** — real GL entries booked in the fiscal year (`get_actual_expense`, L273), and compares the sum against the Budget's annual `budget_amount` and the `get_accumulated_monthly_budget` figure. Each Budget doc configures the outcome per stream via `applicable_on_purchase_order`, `action_if_annual_budget_exceeded_on_po` and `action_if_accumulated_monthly_budget_exceeded_on_po`: **"Stop"** raises `BudgetError` ("Budget Exceeded", via `self.stop()`, L292) which aborts the submit, or **"Warn"** just `msgprint`s. A Company-level `exception_budget_approver_role` downgrades any Stop to a Warn for its holders (`execute_action`, L298). 2. **Authorization Control** — `purchase_order.py:388` calls `AuthorizationControl.validate_approving_authority(doctype, company, base_grand_total)` (`erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154`), which checks `Authorization Rule` records capping the transaction grand total (or discount %) a specific user/role may submit. (Sales Order does the same at `sales_order.py:456` — this is party-agnostic and keyed to the *submitter*.) 3. **Supplier block (the only supplier-level gate, and it isn't a limit)** — the Supplier has `on_hold`, `hold_type` (`"All" / "Invoices" / "Payments"`) and `release_date` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/supplier/supplier.py:60–100`). `AccountsController.ensure_supplier_is_not_blocked()` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:153–170`, invoked from `validate()` at L230 for Purchase Invoice **and** Purchase Order) throws "*{supplier} is blocked so this transaction cannot proceed*" if the supplier is on hold. This runs even on draft save, and it's a binary, time-boxed embargo — no amount is compared. ### How the mechanisms differ in nature | | SO Credit Limit | PO Budget | Authorization Control | Supplier Hold | |---|---|---|---|---| | What it protects | Counterparty credit risk (will the customer pay?) | Internal fiscal discipline (is the spend appropriated?) | Submitter privilege | Business embargo | | Keyed to | The **customer** (Customer → Customer Group → Company limit) | **Expense account × accounting dimension × fiscal period** — the supplier is irrelevant | The **submitting user/role** vs doc grand total | The **supplier**, but as a flag | | Measured against | Accumulated **uncollected exposure**: outstanding receivables (+ optionally unbilled SOs) | Committed + actual spend: unbilled POs + pending MRs + GL actuals, annual and accumulated-monthly | Nothing cumulative — one threshold per rule | No amount at all | | Configurable action | Always blocks non-controllers | **Warn or Stop per Budget doc**; exception approver role | Blocks unless authorized user/role submits | Blocks until released | So the conceptual distinction: a credit limit is an **external, counterparty-risk** control — "this trading partner's aggregate unpaid exposure must not exceed X." The PO-side mechanism is an **internal appropriation/budget** control — "spending against this account/cost-center/project in this period must not exceed the approved envelope, counting both commitments and actuals" — plus a value-based **submitter authority** rule. Neither encodes any property of the supplier; ERPNext simply has no "supplier credit limit" concept, treating supplier risk as a payables/approval problem (holds and authorization) rather than an exposure limit.

## Short answer No — Purchase Order has no per-supplier spend/credit-limit check. There is no "Supplier Credit Limit" equivalent anywhere in the codebase; the amount-based gates that fire when a PO is submitted are **Budget validation** and **Authorization Control**, and both are *internal* controls (company's own budget / user's approval authority), not counterparty exposure controls. ## Where the credit limit actually lives (Sales side) - `SalesOrder.on_submit` → `self.check_credit_limit()` (`erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/sales_order.py:450-452`), which reads the `bypass_credit_limit_check` flag on the `Customer Credit Limit` child table and delegates to `check_credit_limit(customer, company, ...)` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/customer/customer.py:514`. - That function computes `get_credit_limit()` (per-Customer → Customer Group → `Company.credit_limit` fallback, `customer.py:802`), compares it against `get_customer_outstanding()` (GL entries + outstanding SOs + unbilled DNs), and throws *"Credit limit has been crossed for customer {0} ({1}/{2})"* unless the user holds the `credit_controller` role from Accounts Settings. The same check re-fires in `SalesInvoice.on_submit` (`sales_invoice.py:467` → `check_credit_limit` at `:653`). ## What gates Purchase Order submission instead Both run inside `PurchaseOrder.on_submit` (`erpnext/buying/doctype/purchase_order/purchase_order.py:372-392`), so an exception rolls back the submit: **1. Budget check** — `self.validate_budget()` (line 386) → `BuyingController.validate_budget` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:978`): - Default path: `BudgetValidation(doc=self)` (`erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py:13`). For "Purchase Order"/"Material Request" it builds keys of *(dimension, dimension-value, expense_account)* from item rows (Cost Center, Project, plus Accounting Dimensions), fetches submitted `Budget` records with `applicable_on_purchase_order`, then in `validate_for_overbooking` sums the **ordered amount** (POs/MRs, which includes the current doc since PO validation runs after docstatus=1 — see the comment at `budget_controller.py:91-93`) plus **actual GL expense** for the fiscal year, and applies the Budget's `action_if_annual_budget_exceeded_on_po` / `action_if_accumulated_monthly_budget_exceeded_on_po`: **Stop** → `frappe.throw(msg, BudgetError, title="Budget Exceeded")` (`stop()` at line 292), **Warn** → `msgprint`. Users holding the Company's `exception_budget_approver_role` get only a warning (`execute_action`, line 298). - Legacy path (`Accounts Settings.use_legacy_budget_controller`): per-item `validate_expense_against_budget(args)` from `erpnext/accounts/doctype/budget/budget.py:377`, which returns early if no Budget exists at all. **2. Authorization Control** — `frappe.get_cached_doc("Authorization Control").validate_approving_authority(self.doctype, self.company, self.base_grand_total)` (line 388) → `erpnext/setup/doctype/authorization_control/authorization_control.py:154`. It looks up `Authorization Rule` docs for transaction "Purchase Order" matching the submitting user (`system_user`, val=1), the user's roles (`system_role`, val=2) or globally (val=0), with `based_on = "Grand Total"` and a monetary `value` threshold. In `get_appr_user_role` (line 24): if the total exceeds the rule's value and the user has neither the `approving_role` nor is an `approving_user`, it throws *"Not authorized since Grand Total exceeds limits / Can be approved by {roles or users}"*. (Side note: `validate_supplier` (`purchase_order.py:272`) also blocks/warns POs, but via **Supplier Scorecard standing** (`prevent_pos`/`warn_pos`) — a binary quality/standing gate, again not an amount limit.) ## How the nature differs from a credit limit | | Customer credit limit | PO budget check | Authorization Control | |---|---|---|---| | What is measured | The **counterparty's outstanding balance** owed to you (GL receivables + unreconciled SOs + unbilled DNs) | Your **own planned-vs-actual expense** per Cost Center/Project/expense Account | Nothing accumulates — just the **document's grand total vs. a threshold** | | Where the limit is stored | On the party master (`Customer Credit Limit` rows, Customer Group, Company) | On the `Budget` doctype (fiscal year, account, dimension, monthly/annual action) | On `Authorization Rule` (transaction, user/role, value) | | Whose behavior it constrains | The customer's exposure | Company spending, **regardless of supplier** — two POs to different suppliers hitting the same cost center both consume the budget | The **submitting user's authority** | | Override/bypass | `bypass_credit_limit_check` flag, or the `credit_controller` role | `exception_budget_approver_role` on Company (downgrades Stop to Warn) | Having the rule's `approving_role`/`approving_user` | So the asymmetry is deliberate in design: the selling side protects you from a specific customer's accumulating debt, while the buying side has no supplier-risk dial — POs are gated instead by internal fiscal discipline (budget consumption on the expense account/dimension, with Stop/Warn actions) and by approval-authority thresholds on the person submitting.

final answer
## Answer: the premise is inverted — ERPNext doesn't cascade-cancel the invoice, it **blocks** the receipt's cancellation I searched the entire codebase (all `def *cancel*` methods, `doc_events` hooks in `hooks.py`, and every place that queries linked Purchase Invoices), and there is **no method anywhere that cancels a Purchase Invoice as a side-effect of cancelling a Purchase Receipt**. What actually exists is the opposite behavior: a guard that *throws* and prevents the Purchase Receipt from being cancelled while a submitted Purchase Invoice references it. ### The method that enforces consistency: `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` **File:** `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py` (lines 437–450) ```python def on_cancel(self): super().on_cancel() self.check_for_on_hold_or_closed_status("Purchase Order", "purchase_order") # Check if Purchase Invoice has been submitted against current Purchase Order submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) ``` ### How it locates the linked invoice It does **not** use a document link/`get_linked_docs` lookup. It queries the child table **`Purchase Invoice Item`** for any row where: - `purchase_receipt == self.name` (the item-level back-reference to this receipt), and - `docstatus == 1` (the owning invoice is *submitted*), then takes `fields=["parent"]` — the invoice's name — with `limit=1`. If such a row exists, `frappe.throw` raises a `ValidationError` and the receipt cancel aborts. The same query/throw logic also exists as a dedicated helper, **`PurchaseReceipt.check_next_docstatus`** (same file, lines 426–435), covered by the test `test_check_next_docstatus_blocks_with_submitted_invoice` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/test_purchase_receipt.py:6122-6132`. (Note the asymmetry with Delivery Note: `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` at `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:519` actually *calls* its `check_next_docstatus`, whereas the PR inlines the query in `on_cancel`.) ### Why no cascade can happen anyway - `PurchaseReceipt.before_cancel` (line 470) only zeroes `amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice`; `AccountsController.before_cancel` (`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:326`) only validates e-invoice fields — no auto-cancellation. - No `doc_events` hook for Purchase Receipt exists in `erpnext/hooks.py`. - On top of the explicit `frappe.throw`, Frappe's own link validation would also reject the cancel, since a submitted Purchase Invoice still holds a live link to the receipt. ### What the real "stay consistent" flow is You must cancel the **Purchase Invoice first**. `PurchaseInvoice.on_cancel` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/purchase_invoice.py:719-755`) then calls `update_billing_status_for_zero_amount_refdoc("Purchase Receipt")` and `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr()` (defined in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/billing_status.py:21`), which reset `billed_amt`, `per_billed`, and status on the receipt. Only once no submitted invoice references it does `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` proceed to `update_billing_status()` (via `BillingStatusService` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py`) and reverse the stock/GL entries.

final answer
## The premise doesn't hold: ERPNext does not cascade-cancel the invoice — it blocks the receipt cancellation instead I searched the whole call graph (PR `on_cancel`/`before_cancel`, `BuyingController`, `StockController`, `AccountsController`, and every programmatic `.cancel()` call in the codebase) — **there is no method anywhere in ERPNext that automatically cancels a linked Purchase Invoice when a Purchase Receipt is cancelled.** The consistency is enforced the opposite way: the Purchase Receipt simply refuses to be cancelled while a submitted Purchase Invoice references it. ### The method that actually runs on PR cancellation `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel()` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:437-468`: ```python def on_cancel(self): super().on_cancel() self.check_for_on_hold_or_closed_status("Purchase Order", "purchase_order") # Check if Purchase Invoice has been submitted against current Purchase Order submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) ... ``` - **How it locates the linked invoice:** by querying the `Purchase Invoice Item` child table for rows whose `purchase_receipt` field equals the receipt's name and whose parent invoice is submitted (`docstatus == 1`). That back-reference is the link written when a Purchase Invoice is created from a Purchase Receipt. - **What it does with it:** `frappe.throw(...)` — "Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted". The cancellation aborts with a `ValidationError`; the invoice is never touched. The same logic exists as a reusable method, `PurchaseReceipt.check_next_docstatus()` (`purchase_receipt.py:426-435`), which is exercised by the test `test_check_next_docstatus_blocks_with_submitted_invoice` (`test_purchase_receipt.py:6122-6132`) — the docstring there explicitly says the method "**must flag** a submitted Purchase Invoice drawn from the receipt". (In `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` the check is inlined rather than calling `check_next_docstatus()`; in `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` at `delivery_note.py:519` it *is* called, throwing "Sales Invoice {0} has already been submitted" from `DeliveryNote.check_next_docstatus()` at `delivery_note.py:623-640`.) ### How consistency is actually maintained The supported workflow — visible in the tests themselves, e.g. `test_purchase_receipt.py:755-763` and `:1007-1010` — is to cancel in dependency order: **`pi.cancel()` first, then `pr.cancel()`**. Only after the invoice is cancelled does `on_cancel` proceed to: - `self.update_billing_status()` (`purchase_receipt.py:526-527`) → `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py:21-36`, which recomputes `billed_amt` per row and calls `update_billing_percentage()` to reset `per_billed`/status back to "To Bill", - plus `update_prevdoc_status()`, `update_stock_ledger()`, `make_gl_entries_on_cancel()`, etc. Similarly, `BuyingController.on_cancel()` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:959-976`) only handles last-purchase-rate and fixed-asset cleanup for PR/PI — no invoice cancellation there either. So: the method you'd name is `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` (with its helper `check_next_docstatus`), and it finds the invoice via `Purchase Invoice Item.purchase_receipt` + `docstatus == 1` — but it uses that lookup to **prevent** the cancellation with a validation error, not to cascade-cancel the invoice. If a benchmark answer says a method "performs the cascade cancellation," that method does not exist in this codebase.

final answer
I now have the complete picture. Here is the definitive answer: ## Short answer: the premise doesn't match the code — there is no cascade cancellation In this codebase, ERPNext does **not** auto-cancel the linked Purchase Invoice when you cancel a billed Purchase Receipt. Instead, it **blocks the cancellation outright** with a validation error, so the invoice is never left orphaned. (The "cancel linked documents" cascade you may have in mind is the Frappe desk UI's linked-docs dialog, not ERPNext server logic.) ## What actually runs on `PurchaseReceipt.cancel()` **`PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel()`** — `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:437`: ```python def on_cancel(self): super().on_cancel() self.check_for_on_hold_or_closed_status("Purchase Order", "purchase_order") # Check if Purchase Invoice has been submitted against current Purchase Order submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) ... ``` The same lookup is encapsulated in the dedicated helper **`check_next_docstatus()`** (`purchase_receipt.py:426-435`), which raises the identical error. The Delivery Note has the mirrored pattern: `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` (`delivery_note.py:519`) calls its own `check_next_docstatus` (`delivery_note.py:623`). The PR-side helper is covered by `test_check_next_docstatus_blocks_with_submitted_invoice` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/test_purchase_receipt.py:6122`, which asserts the `"...is already submitted"` `ValidationError` is raised. ## How it "locates" the linked invoice Not through a graph traversal or linked-document metadata — through a direct query on the **`Purchase Invoice Item` child table using its `purchase_receipt` link field**. When a Purchase Invoice is created from a receipt, each invoice item row stores the source receipt in `purchase_receipt` (and the specific row in `pr_detail`). The check asks for any row with: - `purchase_receipt == self.name` (the receipt being cancelled) - `docstatus == 1` (submitted invoice only — drafts are ignored) It takes `fields=["parent"]` (the invoice name), `limit=1`, and throws if found. Because of this guard, the cascade-cancel scenario never arises: you must cancel (or amend) the Purchase Invoice first. ## Where the real PR↔PI consistency logic lives After a successful cancel (i.e., when no submitted PI exists), consistency is restored by the billing-status services: - `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py` — `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status()`, `update_billed_amount_based_on_po()` (FIFO allocation of PO-level billed amounts across receipts), and `update_billing_percentage()` (recomputes `per_billed` and `set_status()`), called from `on_cancel` at line 453. - The reverse direction — cancelling a **Purchase Invoice** and pushing the reduced billed amount back into the receipt — is `BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr()` in `erpnext/accounts/doctype/purchase_invoice/services/billing_status.py:21`, invoked from `PurchaseInvoice.on_cancel` (`purchase_invoice.py:740`), with `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel`'s `before_cancel` (`purchase_receipt.py:470-476`) clearing `amount_difference_with_purchase_invoice` per item. So if you were expecting a method like `cancel_purchase_invoices()`, it doesn't exist here — the consistency guarantee is enforced by the `purchase_receipt`-field lookup + `frappe.throw` in `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel` / `check_next_docstatus`, which fails the cancellation before any cascade would be needed.

## Answer **The cascade is not implemented by any ERPNext method — it's performed by the Frappe framework's "auto‑cancel linked documents" behavior that fires on every cancel event.** ERPNext's only involvement is declaring which doctypes must *not* be swept up by it. I verified this across the whole cancel path; here's the complete picture. ### 1. The cascade itself: Frappe's auto-cancel, configured by an ERPNext hook `erpnext/hooks.py:448-461` is the in-repo proof of this mechanism: ```python auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes = [ # On cancel event Payment Entry will be exempted and all linked submittable doctype will get cancelled. # to maintain data integrity we exempted payment entry. it will un-link when sales invoice get cancelled. # if payment entry not in auto cancel exempted doctypes it will cancel payment entry. "Payment Entry", "GL Entry", "Stock Ledger Entry", "Payment Ledger Entry", "Advance Payment Ledger Entry", "Account Closing Balance", ] ``` On a cancel event, the framework cancels **all linked, submitted (docstatus 1) documents** recursively, and skips anything listed in this hook. `Purchase Invoice` is *not* in the exemption list, so cancelling the Purchase Receipt takes the linked submitted Purchase Invoice down with it. (The exemption of `Payment Entry`/GL-type doctypes is why payments are *unlinked* instead — that's the job of `AccountsController.on_cancel` in `erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:1107-1134`, which calls `unlink_ref_doc_from_payment_entries()` when *Accounts Settings → unlink_payment_on_cancellation_of_invoice* is enabled. That method cascades nothing else — it only cancels system-generated Credit/Debit-Note Journal Entries for invoices.) The framework routine lives in frappe itself (the `Document.cancel → _cancel → on_cancel` flow in `frappe/model/document.py`), which isn't part of this repo — hence nothing matching `cancel_linked`/`auto_cancel` exists in ERPNext's Python outside `hooks.py` and the POS-specific `POSInvoiceMergeLog.cancel_linked_invoices()` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/pos_invoice_merge_log/pos_invoice_merge_log.py:421`). ### 2. How the linked invoice is located The framework walks **incoming standard link fields** — doctypes whose Link fields point *at* the cancelled Purchase Receipt. For the invoice, that field is **`Purchase Invoice Item.purchase_receipt`**. You can see ERPNext performing exactly this lookup itself in **`PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel`** (`erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/purchase_receipt.py:437-450`): ```python def on_cancel(self): super().on_cancel() self.check_for_on_hold_or_closed_status("Purchase Order", "purchase_order") # Check if Purchase Invoice has been submitted against current Purchase Order submitted = frappe.get_all( "Purchase Invoice Item", filters={"purchase_receipt": self.name, "docstatus": 1}, fields=["parent"], as_list=True, limit=1, ) if submitted: frappe.throw(_("Purchase Invoice {0} is already submitted").format(submitted[0][0])) ``` Note the subtlety: **ERPNext does not use this lookup to cascade — it uses it as a guard that *throws***. The two mechanisms compose: once the framework has auto-cancelled the linked submitted invoice (docstatus → 2), this `docstatus: 1` query finds nothing, the guard passes, and the PR cancellation proceeds cleanly. It's the safety net if a submitted PI still references the PR when the hook runs (e.g. server-side cancels that bypass the framework flow). ### 3. Corroborating evidence (same pattern on the sales side) - `DeliveryNote.on_cancel` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:515-542`) calls `check_next_docstatus()` (defined at line 623), which throws `"Sales Invoice {0} is already submitted"` using the identical lookup pattern — `Sales Invoice Item` filtered by `delivery_note: self.name, docstatus: 1`. Same design: framework cascades, ERPNext guards. - `BuyingController.on_cancel` (`erpnext/controllers/buying_controller.py:959-976`) only refreshes last purchase rates and deletes linked assets — no invoice cascade. - After the cascade, ERPNext restores billing consistency via `update_prevdoc_status()` / `update_billing_status()` and `update_billing_percentage()` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/purchase_receipt/services/billing_status.py:172`, which recomputes `per_billed` on the PR once the invoice's billed amounts are rolled back (`BillingStatusService.update_billing_status_in_pr()` from `PurchaseInvoice.on_cancel`, `purchase_invoice.py:719-773`). ### Summary - **Which method:** none in ERPNext — the cascade is the Frappe framework's auto-cancel of linked submittable documents on the cancel event (frappe/model/document.py cancel flow), enabled/curated from ERPNext via the `auto_cancel_exempted_doctypes` hook (`erpnext/hooks.py:448`). - **How it locates the linked invoice:** by reverse link-field lookup — submitted `Purchase Invoice` documents whose items reference the receipt through `Purchase Invoice Item.purchase_receipt` (the very same query ERPNext duplicates as a blocking guard in `PurchaseReceipt.on_cancel`, `purchase_receipt.py:442-450`).

## Answer The check lives in **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** in **`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py` (lines 295–349)** — it runs during `validate()` (which Frappe also triggers on submit), so a `frappe.throw` there blocks the submission entirely. ### Call chain for Sales Invoice / Delivery Note 1. `SalesInvoice` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62`, `class SalesInvoice(SellingController)`) and `DeliveryNote` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17`, `class DeliveryNote(SellingController)`) both inherit from `SellingController`. 2. `SellingController.validate()` (`selling_controller.py:60-77`) first calls `super().validate()` → `AccountsController.validate()`, which at **`erpnext/controllers/accounts_controller.py:244`** calls `self.set_incoming_rate()`. 3. `SellingController.set_incoming_rate()` (`selling_controller.py:515-676`) then fills `incoming_rate` on each item row for **Delivery Note** always, and **Sales Invoice only when `update_stock=1`** (line 543), by pulling the item's actual valuation via `get_incoming_rate()` (FIFO/valuation rate from stock ledger, `get_rate_for_return()` for returns). 4. Back in `SellingController.validate()`, `self.validate_selling_price()` (line 65) runs **after** `super().validate()`, so the incoming rates are already populated. ### What the check does (`selling_controller.py:295-349`) - **Gate:** returns immediately unless **`Selling Settings.validate_selling_price`** ("Validate selling price for Item against purchase or valuation rate", defined in `erpnext/selling/doctype/selling_settings/selling_settings.json:155`) is enabled; also skipped for returns (`is_return`), internal customers, free items, and non-stock items (lines 315–336). - **Comparison 1 — purchase cost:** fetches `last_purchase_rate` (adjusted by `conversion_factor`) from the Item master and throws if `base_net_rate` is lower (lines 324–333). - **Comparison 2 — valuation:** for `Sales Invoice`/`Delivery Note` it compares `base_net_rate` against the row's **`incoming_rate`**; for `Sales Order`/`Quotation` it uses `valuation_rate` instead (line 338: `rate_field = "valuation_rate" if self.doctype in ["Sales Order", "Quotation"] else "incoming_rate"`). - **Blocking:** both violations go through the nested `throw_message()` (lines 296–313), which calls `frappe.throw(..., title="Invalid Selling Price")` with: *"Row #N: Selling rate for item X is lower than its valuation rate/last purchase rate. Selling net rate should be at least Y. Alternatively, you can disable 'Validate selling price…' in Selling Settings to bypass this validation."* ### Related pieces - Tests proving the block: `test_validate_selling_price` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/test_delivery_note.py:3451` (rate 9 vs. incoming rate 10 → `dn.save()` raises `frappe.ValidationError`; setting `incoming_rate = 0` bypasses it). - The same validation is re-applied when child items are amended on ordered/submitted docs via `update_child_qty_rate` → `parent.validate_selling_price()` in `erpnext/accounts/services/child_item_update.py:174`. - `POSInvoice` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/pos_invoice/pos_invoice.py:33`) extends `SalesInvoice`, so it inherits the same check.

## Short answer The block lives in one shared server-side method: **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** in **`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py` (lines 295–349)**. It runs from the framework `validate` hook, so it fires before any draft can be saved or submitted — which is exactly where the submission gets blocked. ## How the flow works **1. Controller inheritance (who gets the check)** - `class DeliveryNote(SellingController)` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17` - `class SalesInvoice(SellingController)` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62` - (also `SalesOrder` and `Quotation`) **2. Entry point — `SellingController.validate()`** (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:60–70`, check at line 65): ```python def validate(self): super().validate() ... self.validate_selling_price() ``` **3. The actual validation — `validate_selling_price()`** (lines 295–349): - First it bails out if the doc is a return (`is_return`) or if the feature toggle is off (line 315): ```python if self.get("is_return") or not frappe.get_single_value("Selling Settings", "validate_selling_price"): return ``` - For each item row (skipping blank rows and free items) it compares the item's **`base_net_rate`** (net selling rate in company currency, adjusted by `conversion_factor`) against two reference costs: - **`last_purchase_rate`** from the Item master (lines 324–333) - For stock items sold to non-internal customers, the **item's actual valuation/cost** — the rate field is chosen per doctype (line 338): `valuation_rate` for `Sales Order`/`Quotation`, and **`incoming_rate`** for `Delivery Note`/`Sales Invoice` (the `incoming_rate` on the row is the stock's valuation rate, populated via `get_incoming_rate` in `erpnext/stock/utils.py`). ```python if item.get(rate_field) and item.base_net_rate < (valuation_rate := flt(item.get(rate_field) * ...)): throw_message(..., "valuation rate") ``` - On failure it calls the nested `throw_message()` helper (lines 296–313), which raises `frappe.throw(...)` → a `frappe.ValidationError` titled **"Invalid Selling Price"**: *"Row #N: Selling rate for item X is lower than its valuation rate. Selling net rate should be at least Y. Alternatively, you can disable 'Validate Selling Price' in Selling Settings to bypass this validation."* Because this happens inside `validate`, Frappe aborts the save/submit — the document can never reach submitted state. **4. ## Answer The check lives in one shared place: **`SellingController.validate_selling_price()`** in `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py` (line 295). ### The call chain 1. Both documents inherit from `SellingController`: - `class SalesInvoice(SellingController)` — `erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62` - `class DeliveryNote(SellingController)` — `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17` 2. `SellingController.validate()` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:60`) calls `self.validate_selling_price()` at **line 65**, so the block fires during document validation (i.e., on Submit, and on Save too), throwing a `frappe.throw` which aborts the submission. 3. There's also a secondary trigger point: `erpnext/accounts/services/child_item_update.py:174` re-invokes `parent.validate_selling_price()` when child item rows are updated. ### What it validates (lines 295–349) For each non-free item row, it compares the item's **`base_net_rate`** against two floors: 1. **`Item.last_purchase_rate`** (converted to the sales UOM via `conversion_factor`) — checked for **all** items. 2. **Valuation cost** — only for **stock items** sold to non-internal customers. The rate field chosen is doctype-dependent (line 338): - `incoming_rate` for **Delivery Note** and **Sales Invoice** (the item row's incoming/valuation rate), - `valuation_rate` for Sales Order and Quotation. ### Skip conditions (line 315) - `self.get("is_return")` — returns are exempt (as are debit notes / internal customers per lines 63, 318, 335) - The whole check is **gated by the `validate_selling_price` checkbox in Selling Settings**: `frappe.get_single_value("Selling Settings", "validate_selling_price")`. If the setting is off, no block happens. ### The blocking message When the rate is below cost, it throws with `title=_("Invalid Selling Price")`: > *Row #X: Selling rate for item {item} is lower than its {last purchase rate / valuation rate}. Selling net rate should be at least {rate}. Alternatively, you can disable 'Validate Selling Price' in Selling Settings to bypass this validation.* ### Where it's exercised - `test_validate_selling_price` in `erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/test_delivery_note.py:3452` (with `@change_settings("Selling Settings", {"validate_selling_price": 1})`) - A similar test in `erpnext/selling/doctype/sales_order/test_sales_order.py:2786` So in short: it's not duplicated per-doctype — the guard is the single `validate_selling_price()` method on `SellingController` (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:295`), controlled by the **"Validate Selling Price"** checkbox in Selling Settings, and it's inherited by both Sales Invoice and Delivery Note.

## The block: `SellingController.validate_selling_price()` — `erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:295` ### Where the check lives The loss-selling guard is a single method, **`validate_selling_price()`** (`erpnext/controllers/selling_controller.py:295-349`), defined on the shared **`SellingController`** base class (`selling_controller.py:19`). It's invoked from **`SellingController.validate()`** at **line 65**: ```python def validate(self): # selling_controller.py:60 super().validate() self.validate_items() if not (self.get("is_debit_note") or self.get("is_return")): self.validate_max_discount() self.validate_selling_price() # line 65 — the gate ... ``` Both doctorms you asked about reach it through this chain: - **Sales Invoice** — `class SalesInvoice(SellingController)` (`erpnext/accounts/doctype/sales_invoice/sales_invoice.py:62`); `SalesInvoice.validate()` (line 289) calls `super().validate()`. - **Delivery Note** — `class DeliveryNote(SellingController)` (`erpnext/stock/doctype/delivery_note/delivery_note.py:17`), so it inherits the same `validate()`. Because Frappe runs `validate()` on both save and submit, the `frappe.throw` here blocks the submission with a **"Invalid Selling Price"** validation error. ### What it checks, per item row - **Gate** (line 315): skipped entirely if the doc is a return (`is_return`) or unless the Selling Settings checkbox is on: `frappe.get_single_value("Selling Settings", "validate_selling_price")`. - Free items are skipped (line 321). - It fetches the item's `last_purchase_rate` and `is_stock_item` (line 324-326) and converts it to the sales UOM via `conversion_factor` (lines 328-330). - **Purchase-cost check** (lines 332-333): if `item.base_net_rate < last_purchase_rate_in_sales_uom` → throw *"Selling rate for item … is lower than its last purchase rate"*. - For internal customers or non-stock items it skips the valuation check (`continue`, lines 335-336). - **Valuation check** (lines 338-349): the reference field is `incoming_rate` for Sales Invoice and Delivery Note (the stock valuation rate at delivery/invoicing time), `valuation_rate` for Sales Order/Quotation. If `base_net_rate < incoming_rate × conversion_factor` → throw *"…lower than its valuation rate"*. The nested `throw_message()` helper (lines 296-313) raises the error, whose message explicitly points users to the bypass: *"Alternatively, you can disable 'Validate selling price for Item against purchase or valuation rate' in Selling Settings."* ### The enabling setting The block is **off by default** — it's controlled by the Check field `validate_selling_price` in `erpnext/selling/doctype/selling_settings/selling_settings.json` (lines 152-158): *"Enable this to block transactions where the selling price is less than the purchase or valuation rate"* (default `0`), on the **Selling Settings** form. ### Other call site `validate_selling_price` is also re-run when items are edited post-creation: `erpnext/accounts/services/child_item_update.py:174` calls `parent.validate_selling_price()` in `_post_update` when replacing a Sales Order's items via the Update Items flow. (Note: `POSInvoice(SalesInvoice)` inherits the same check; `SalesOrder`/`Quotation` get the `valuation_rate` variant of the check.)
